articleTitle: Deep Spectrogram Feature Based ECG Signal Quality Assessment for False Alarm Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) based continuous monitoring of vital signs and disease detection devices are susceptible to artifacts while recording the signals. Noisy ECG signal analysis for vital sign monitoring generates false alarms. There is a requirement for quality-aware health monitoring devices to reduce false alarms. The ECG signal quality assessment method contributes to efficient power utilization in resource-constrained wearable devices. This paper proposes an automatic, lightweight, and energy-efficient ECG signal quality assessment method based on spectrogram and convolutional neural network (CNN). For the optimal method, 24 CNNs are trained and tested. The CNNs are with 2, 3, and 4 numbers of convolutional layers; six different kernel sizes; and dense layers of 3 and 4. The optimal CNN for the quality assessment ECG signal has three convolutional layers, three dense layers, and a kernel size of $6\times 6$. For a database unseen to the optimal CNN, the method has a sensitivity of 95.01% and a specificity of 95%. The optimal CNN has a testing time or latency of 18.49 ms for quality assessment of a 5 s ECG signal. The model size of the spectrogram and CNN-based optimal ECG signal quality assessment method is 723 kB.

articleTitle: A Fine-Tuned MobileNetv2 based Approach for Weed Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Weed Detection and classification plays a very crucial role in farming. Manually detecting weeds accurately and spraying herbicides exactly to the weed location is a challenge. Hence, there is a need for automation in weed detection. With the advancements in the field of computer vision, machine learning and deep learning, extensive research has been carried out in this field to accurately detect weeds and spray herbicides on the exact location of weeds so that the crops don’t get affected. It also aids in preventing health and environment hazards caused due to the unwanted spraying of herbicides. Hence, this paper proposes a fine-tuned MobileNetv2 based solution for automatic weed detection and classification in images. The proposed work transfer learns the rich feature extraction from the pre-trained MobileNetv2 architecture and fine-tunes the last layers of the model on DeepWeed dataset by considering a variety of optimizers and activation functions. The proposed work compares the performance of the fine-tuned model against several state-of-art algorithms on the DeepWeeds benchmark dataset. The results show that the proposed model outperforms other state-of-art methods.

articleTitle: MFAAN: Unveiling Audio Deepfakes with a Multi-Feature Authenticity Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the contemporary digital age, the proliferation of deepfakes presents a formidable challenge to the sanctity of information dissemination. Audio deepfakes, in particular, can be deceptively realistic, posing significant risks in misinformation campaigns. To address this threat, we introduce the Multi-Feature Audio Authenticity Network (MFAAN)—an advanced architecture tailored for the detection of fabricated audio content. MFAAN incorporates multiple parallel paths designed to harness the strengths of different audio representations, including Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) [1], linear-frequency cepstral coefficients (LFCC) [1], and Chroma Short Time Fourier Transform (Chroma-STFT). By synergistically fusing these features, MFAAN achieves a nuanced understanding of audio content, facilitating robust differentiation between genuine and manipulated recordings. Preliminary evaluations of MFAAN on two benchmark datasets, ‘In-the-Wild’ Audio Deepfake Data [2] and The Fake-or-Real Dataset [3], demonstrate its superior performance, achieving accuracies of 98.93% and 94.47% respectively. Such results not only underscore the efficacy of MFAAN but also highlight its potential as a pivotal tool in the ongoing battle against deepfake audio content.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Circularly Polarized RFID Reader Antenna for Internet of Things Application
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article proposes a unique approach to design RFID Reader antenna for Internet of things applications. Here a circular patch with two orthogonal slots etched on the patch is used to acquire UHF RFID band at 915 MHz and WLAN band at 2.45 GHz. Four slits on the ground plane are etched to improve the axial ratio. To minimize the back lobe and enhance the gain at both bands, we have employed a dual-band AMC reflector. Our results show the simulated 3dB axial ratio bandwidths of 4.2% and 2.1% at UHF and WLAN bands respectively with gains of 4.5dBi and 7.2dBi. This antenna system is ideal for IoT applications.

articleTitle: Multimodal Biometric Authentication based on Score Level Fusion of Palmprint and Iris
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Biometrics is a highly used technology which is earning research interest from past many years due to its applications in access control, identification, forensic investigation and surveillance. In this work, due to the inherent advantages of multimodal system over unimodal system, a multimodal system is proposed. Two or more biometric modalities when combined, offer more reliable identification and verification system. Here, palmprint and iris are used in identification due to its high robustness. Feature extraction methods used are average absolute deviation (AAD), histogram of gradients (HOG), and Gaussian membership feature (GMF) over both the modalities. K-nearest neighbor (KNN) classifier is used for matching with Euclidean distance. Finally, score level fusion is performed using frank T-norm, Schweizer-Sklar, Hamacher norm and Dubois-Prade fusion rules. The results show the robustness of the proposed fusion techniques over individual modality recognition rate.

articleTitle: Deep Transfer Learning for Tomato Leaf Diseases Detection and Classification using Pre-trained Models
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Tomatoes are among the most important and widespread crops worldwide. The amount of tomatoes produced varies according to the method of fertilization used. Leaf diseases are the key reason affecting both the quantity and quality of crop yields. Consequently, it is important to diagnose and classify these diseases in the early stages. Recent advances in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated excellent performance in solving image diagnosis and classification tasks in computer vision. Transfer Learning offers an efficient and cost-effective approach to building deep CNNs. In this work transfer learning approaches were applied to accurately classify the tomato leaf diseases. VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 models were tuned up and customized for transfer learning. Plant Village Dataset was used in this research work which consists of a total of 16,012 images belonging to 9 disease classes and 1 healthy class. The results indicate that VGG 16, when used in conjunction with transfer learning, outperformed both VGG19 and Resnet50, achieving a superior training accuracy of 95.1%.

articleTitle: Tomato Leaf Disease Classification with Lightweight Federated Learning using Identically Distributed Images
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Tomatoes grown and consumed extensively in Asia are an essential source of protein (22% per Tomato) and energy (18% per Tomato). Bacterial, fungal, and other microbial diseases severely impact plant health and productivity for tomato farmers. Manual diagnosis of many diseases is challenging, especially in places that need access to crop protection experts. Automated disease identification is crucial for Tomato leaf protection and reduced crop loss. Unfortunately, no one method of categorizing leaf diseases in tomatoes has proven to be consistently accurate enough for widespread usage. The present study offers a streamlined federated deep learning framework to classify tomato leaf diseases while ensuring the preservation of sensitive data. This framework safeguards client information with a decentralized client-server architecture and verifies federated deep learning models with IID. The researchers piloted the framework with a single and several clients in both conventional and federated learning environments. After extracting features from numerous pre-trained models, AlexNet is selected as baseline because of its superior 99.53% accuracy. Next, IID datasets were put through their paces using federal learning (FL). The extra capabilities of the framework make it the ideal option for early Tomato leaf disease categorization.

articleTitle: Development of a LiFi System for Under Water Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Underwater communication often faces challenges due to the significant attenuation of radio frequency (RF) waves at the higher end, which is necessary for high-speed data transfer in aquatic environments. For crucial underwater operations, a dependable communication link is essential, especially for transmitting urgent alerts. The solution might lie in LiFi technology, which leverages Visible Light Communication (VLC) to achieve rapid data transmission using light sources. This study suggests a communication system based on LiFi principles tailored for short-distance underwater communication. The document begins by shedding light on LiFi technology, contrasting its merits with conventional wireless communication systems. It also addresses the constraints of LiFi, particularly its limited range underwater. The proposed system is detailed in the study and includes a transmission unit, a reception unit, and dual operational modes—textual and auditory. A swimming pool with a distance adjustment setup is utilized for the experiment. The system also boasts two practical applications: an SOS signal function and a remote control feature for underwater equipment. The study concludes with a comprehensive discussion on the functioning of the recommended system and its prospective utility in diverse sectors.

articleTitle: Prediction of Protein Biomarkers for Mycobacterium fortuitum using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: M. fortuitum is a recognized rapidly growing bacterium known for causing opportunistic infections in humans. Understanding the pathophysiology of M. fortuitum requires analysis of genes and proteins involved in the growth and multiplication of the bacilli. Global proteome analysis of the bacteria was done in triplicate (P1, P2, and P3). Utilizing the proteome dataset of M. fortuitum, neural network (NN) analysis, a machine learning technique, was utilized to find the differential expression profile of proteins for the first time in order to develop a model that aids in the prediction of biomarkers. Moreover, employing NN analysis yielded a prediction model that was more precise and effective than those derived from conventional techniques, underscoring the potential of this approach to promote the identification of biomarkers for infectious illnesses. The mean square error and coefficient of determination were calculated for each of the three data sets. The model which had various levels of protein expression was evaluated. As a consequence of the investigation, the model with greater protein expression levels results lower mean square error values and higher coefficient of determination values. P1 was tested to see if it met the requirements for training data for more combinations using the P2 and P3 sets. This implies that adding additional information on protein expression enhances the prediction model’s ability to accurately identify potential biomarkers in bacterial diseases like M. fortuitum.

articleTitle: MineralNet: A Composite Deep Learning Model for Accurate Classification and Identification of Minerals Using CNN-SVM Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The identification and categorization of minerals are crucial processes in many fields of geology and mining. To accurately classify and identify minerals, this research introduces a unique composite deep learning model named MineralNet, which combines the best features of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM). Specifically, 5,640 high-resolution images of minerals are used to train and assess the proposed model. An outstanding 98.8% accuracy on the mineral dataset was achieved using the suggested composite model. This outperforms conventional machine learning methods, demonstrating the power of the CNN-SVM fusion technique in mineral categorization. When tested on real-world mineral datasets, the model also shows signs of stability and generalizability, highlighting its potential for use in geological research and mining.

articleTitle: Classification of NFR based Importance Level of User Story in Agile Software Development
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The fact that requirement engineering creates effective technology and prevents system failure is very important in the early phases of software development. The final implementation criteria and the selection of many alternative models both heavily depend on non-functional requirements. The term "non-functional requirements" (NFR) refers to a group of qualities that software must possess, such as security, dependability, performance, etc. Extracting and considering NFR from user stories in Agile Software Development (ASD) can help developers deliver quality software that meets the expectations of users completely. This paper proposed the classification of NFR based importance level of user story in ASD using machine learning models. At the beginning of this work, requirement converted into user stories, then the weight of NFR type and importance level of each user story calculated and classified using machine learning models. The outcome of this work shows that random forest classifier and XGBoost are achieved the best results with an accuracy of 96.39% and decision tree classifier accuracy is 96.13%, with comparisons of K-nearest neighbor, linear discriminant analysis, support vector classifier, logistic regression, and naïve bayes.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Step-down Switched Capacitor DC-DC Converter for SoC
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: As a subset of DC-DC power converters, switched capacitor (SC) converters solely employ switches and capacitors are effective in converting one voltage to another. For two-phase 2:1 SC converters, this paper provides an exhaustive analysis and approach for efficiency improvement. First, different parameters modeled by implementing them into the dual-phase 2:1 series parallel SC converter to make a realizable design. To get an optimized efficiency value, several influences on efficiency investigated by adjusting switch resistance, load resistance, switching frequency, capacitor area, and switch area. There is a good correlation between the analysis conclusions and those from the simulation. Simulation and MATLAB modeling used for the validation of this analysis technique.

articleTitle: Eight-Element Low-Profile MIMO System for Thin 5G Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study introduces an eight element antenna array for ultrathin smartphones that works on LTE 42 band(3.4GHz3.6GHz). On the two side frames, which measure 140 $\times 4 \times 0.8$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the antenna elements are evenly distributed. The MIMO array is placed on the circuit board of dimension 150 $\times 75 \times 0.8$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. There is enough space between antennas to achieve 13.5dB isolation. Efficiency is also better than 51%. The proposed design an excellent option for ultrathin smartphone applications as it provides high isolation and compact size.

articleTitle: Smart Precision Farming in Substrate Medium - A Practical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The use of IoT in agricultural processes has gained increased importance due to the enhanced production and the efficient monitoring of the farming setup. The plant growth can be monitored and controlled using smart setups including sensors, and other hardware components. The growth requirements of the plants can be altered according to their requirements. The real-time data is collected from sensors and it can be sent to the cloud for analysis. If any of the growth condition is seen to be violated, the corresponding conditions can be checked and altered. This was the cultivation process called smart precision farming. The analysis can be predictive as well. The historical data can be analyzed by the cloud to predict weather conditions, irrigation needs, etc. accurately. This plays a very crucial role in smart precision farming because it helps farmers to make informed decisions that affect crop production. All this information can be accessed through an end device via a mobile or web application. A setup has been created by the authors to monitor the growth conditions of a plant cultivated in the smart setup where the growing conditions of the plant are monitored and controlled for optimal resource utilization and enhanced yield.

articleTitle: Single and Dual Horn SIW Radiators for High Speed Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: High speed vehicular communication requires high data rate and high capacity antennas for the mmW 5G applications. Multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antennas have high data rates and high capacity. When substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is combined with the MIMO antennas penetration losses and reliability issues can be minimized in high speed vehicles like high-speed trains, airplanes, satellites, and in underground moving vehicles. The proposed design consists of single and dual H-plane horns on multilayer substrates Rogers RT5880 and Rogers RO3003 of sizes $56.32 \times 35.06$ square meter and $56.74 \times 34.72$ square meter. The single horn MIMO radiator covers a wide band of 26.36-35.32 GHz (Bandwidth = 8.96 GHz), has radiation efficiency in the range 95.82%-97.93%, and gain in the range 6.7 – 9.15 dBi. The dual horn MIMO radiator covers a wide band of 26.63-35.32 GHz frequency range (Bandwidth $=8.69$ GHz), has radiation efficiency in range 96.10%-97.90%, and 6.94-8.93 dBi gain in the whole $2:1$ voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) band. The envelope correlation coefficient in both the radiators lies in the range 0-0.0012.

articleTitle: Incorporating Requirement Engineering into Agile Methodologies: Challenges and Proposed Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Agile software development has a good track record, but only when the project size is limited. Requirement engineering (RE) is critical because “Requirements” play a critical role at each stage of the lifecycle of software. Agile supports changing customer requirements while adding value to the business, it also comes with its own set of obstacles, many of which are connected to requirement constraints. This study seeks to uncover the issues that agile project requirements engineers confront. Many research studies on requirement issues have been undertaken, all of which are compromised in some way, offer no suggestions for improving the agile development process, and fail to reveal massive agile development hurdles. This paper addresses all the issues raised above and suggests possible solutions from the standpoint of requirement engineering and results can be extremely beneficial to the software business in terms of improving development processes, as well as individuals who would like to continue working in this area.

articleTitle: Reduction of Subthreshold Leakage Using Metal Strip in SGO Double-Gate MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper investigates and compares the reduction of subthreshold leakage current ISUB in the stack-gate-oxide double-gate metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (SGO-DG-MOSFET) and stack-gate-oxide low work function live-strip double gate MOSFET (SGO-LWLS-DG-MOSFET). A comparative discussion is carried out in the simulation results using the technology computer-aided design (TCAD) tool. Reduction in ISUB of $10^{-3}\mathrm{A}/\mu \mathrm{m}$ is observed in SGO-LWLS-DG-MOSFET compared to SGO-DG-MOSFET. However, 11.23% enhancement is noticed in the transconductance $\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{m}}$ of SGO-LWLS-DG-MOSFET. Due to the low ISUB, SGO-LWLS-DG-MOSFET exhibits a considerable improvement in the switching ratio as well.

articleTitle: A Blockchain Application for Secure Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Collaboration is a communication process in which two or more people, teams, or organizations work together to achieve a common goal. Users in the collaboration expect communication to be secure and trustworthy so that essential information may be exchanged appropriately and the risk of sensitive information leakage is avoided. When communication takes place in a public setting and money is involved, trust and security in the partnership become even more vital. Blockchain technology has attracted a lot of attention in recent years because it guarantees trust and security during communication. It was found to be more appropriate for decentralized applications in which communicating entities do not know each other but want to establish trusted communication and interact with one another. To this end, this paper presents the design and implementation of smart contracts for the blockchain-based secure collaboration to ensure trustworthy communication across users where money is involved. The proposed application is developed on the Ethereum blockchain framework as it offers secure communication and currency. Also, we present the web application that implements the proposed model.

articleTitle: Prediction of Handwritten Classification using CNN Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Today’s computer vision industry makes extensive use of image recognition. A popular method of image recognition is digit recognition. The recognition of handwritten numbers is one of the most well-known difficulties in computer vision and machine learning applications. In essence, this model proposes an online approach for recognizing handwritten digits (HDR) by utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNN).As a training sample, the technique uses the MINST dataset, which contains centered 28x28 gray scale images of handwritten numbers. It has 10,000 test cases and 60,000 training examples. This paper shows the accuracy rate and loss of the model. Lastly, execute the trials using a variety of random handwritten 28x28 pixel digits.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of CMOS Based Voltage Reference Circuits in 180nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The accurate and stable generation of reference voltages is vital in low power VLSI circuit applications. In this paper, a performance comparison of CMOS-based voltage reference circuits implemented in 180nm technology node is evaluated. The study’s goal is to assess and compare the efficiency metrics of several voltage reference circuits in order to help circuit designers choose the best appropriate circuit for their specific requirements. The findings of the study have the potential to impact circuit design practices and improve the accuracy and stability of voltage references in analog and mixed signal integrated circuits. The result also highlights the potential trade-offs for further optimization in future circuit designs.

articleTitle: Implementation of 1-bit Full Adder using Various Low Power Techniques on 45nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Full Adder is the most commonly used digital component, with applications in arithmetic implementations, processors, digital filters, etc. It plays a critical role in determining the overall power of a digital system, so the reduction in power for this component can reduce the power of the overall system drastically. This paper implements and compares various low-power techniques suggested for a 1-bit full adder. These techniques usually revolve around logic style, hybrid digital styles, redundant components, and reduced transistor count techniques. In this paper, three types of techniques are discussed. The Gate-diffused Input (GDI) technique aims to lower the voltage swing for power reduction [1]. Using redundant components like multiplexers can comparatively reduce power, and decrease the circuit complexity [2]. Mixing of different techniques is also possible, this can be seen in hybrid module implementation [3]. All these different techniques are implemented at 45nm process node, in Cadence Virtuoso. The results for the same were analyzed, tabulated, and compared. Further, a layout for a 16T hybrid full adder was prepared after which post-layout simulations were performed and the results were compared. Monte Carlo analysis was also performed for observing the average power consumption in 16T hybrid full adder.

articleTitle: Analyzing Social Media texts for Suicidal Risk Identification using Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Suicide is a pressing public health concern, with nearly 700,000 people taking their own lives annually, equating to one life lost every 45 seconds as per the World Health Organization. Recognizing that individuals contemplating suicide may exhibit identifiable behavioral patterns prior to their attempts, this work aims to employ Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithms for prediction of risk of committing suicide by analyzing these patterns in social media posts. The system presented in this study uses machine learning to predict and identify suicidal ideation in online social content. To detect suicidal ideas via digital communication, the framework uses machine learning approaches. In this work, the machine learning algorithms SVM, logistic regression and CNN provide accuracy of 94.02%, 93.7% and 92.09% respectively.

articleTitle: Quantifying NBTI Recovery and Its Impact on Lifetime Estimations in Advanced Semiconductor Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Understanding the impact of recovery on Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) measurements has remained a persistent challenge in accurately estimating the reliability life-time of semiconductor devices. Despite significant efforts to mitigate this influence, achieving its complete elimination has proven elusive. This paper aims to quantify the extent of recovery’s effect on NBTI measurements and subsequently investigates how the choice of measurement system and testing duration influence NBTI lifetime estimation in advanced technologies such as 22nm Bulk CMOS and 22nm Metal Gate High-k (MGK) Technologies. These insights are pivotal for enhancing our comprehension of NBTI behavior and improving the reliability assessment of cutting-edge semiconductor technologies.

articleTitle: Gain and Directivity Enhancement of mm-wave MIMO Array for 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: For 5G wireless applications, a single-patch antenna with a ring-shaped slot and a $1 \times 8$ Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna array is proposed. The substrate is comprised of FR4 material, and it has a dielectric constant of 4.4 and a thickness of 1 mm. A very small rectangular microstrip patch antenna with measurements of 1.977 mm by 3.5 mm by 01 mm is used in the proposed MIMO antenna array. For resonating frequency, performance metrics such as return loss, bandwidth, antenna gain, antenna efficiency, and VSWR are computed. The proposed MIMO antenna array has a return loss of less than -10 dB and resonates at 26 GHz frequency. The proposed MIMO array has a maximum possible antenna gain directivity of 7.59 dB respectively for the resonant frequency and an antenna efficiency of 90 %. The VSWR for the MIMO array lies between 0 to 2. This proposed antenna array might be appropriate for a variety of high-frequency applications because of its improved qualities.

articleTitle: Design of SIW based Hexagonal Patch Filtering Antenna for n-77 and n-78 Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A low-profile single-layer substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) filtering antenna with higher realized gain and low circuit profile is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is comprised of a hexagonal patch and rectangular SIW cavity with a hexagonal slot and a split-ring slot etched on the top surface of the substrate. The composite structure is intended to offer three modes within the passband in order to achieve a wider impedance bandwidth. The radiation null near lower band-edge is originated using the hexagonal slot, while the null near the upper band-edge frequency is implemented using the hexagonal patch. Surface current distribution exposes current cancellation and null generation. The proposed filtering antenna has a compact size of $0.893 \lambda_{0} \times 0.608 \lambda_{0}$. The simulated −10 dB impedance bandwidth ranges from 3.70 to 3.91 GHz (5.5%) with realized gain of 7.5 dB at a center frequency of 3.8 GHz. The out-of-band suppression level is higher than 11.77 dB in 1-3.68 GHz and more than 17.19 dB in 3.98-6 GHz.

articleTitle: Outage Analysis of Single-Stage Relay NOMA Over Power Line Communication Under Impulsive Noise
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, we study and present the performance based on the outage probability of a single-stage, relay-aided, cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access over power line communication under a Bernoulli-Gaussian impulsive noise. The network setup comprises one source node and two destination nodes, among which one of the nodes closer to the source acts as a relay, transmitting a symbol from the source node to the destination. The relay considered is a decoded-and-forward relay, which helps to transmit the source symbol to the destination over two-time frames. We derive the mathematical expressions to determine outage probabilities at the relay and destination nodes within the studied network. Furthermore, we develop an optimization problem related to the power distribution coefficient at the source, deriving the corresponding mathematical expressions. To validate our analysis, we employ simulations and numerical methods.

articleTitle: Improved Ensemble based Transfer Learning Approach for Indian Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition is the task of automatically recognizing ISL signs from images. This is a challenging task due to the large variability in ISL signs, the limited availability of ISL datasets, and the dynamic nature of sign language. Transfer learning is a method which can be used to improve the performance of ISL recognition models. Transfer learning implies using a pre-trained model that has been trained on a large dataset of images. The pre-trained model is then fine-tuned on a smaller dataset of ISL images. However, Ensemble learning is a technique that can be used to improve the recognition accuracy as it combines the predictions of multiple models to produce a single prediction. This study presents a collection of transfer learning techniques for the recognition of ISL. The proposed approach employs three pre-trained models, specifically ResNet50, VGG16, and InceptionV3. Using a dataset of ISL images, the pre-trained models are fine-tuned. Subsequently, the ensemble learning technique is employed to combine the predictions generated by the three models. Here, ensemble is based on a weighted voting method. The performance of the proposed framework has been quantitatively analyzed on multiple evaluation parameters to demonstrate its effectiveness for ISL recognition.

articleTitle: Security Analysis of A Mixed RF-FSO-VLC Triple Hop Cooperative Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research investigates a mixed radio frequency (RF)-free space optic (FSO)-visible light communications (VLC) cooperative relaying system that allows communication from an outside to an indoor system. In this case, the FSO link serves as a bridge between the core RF link and the last mile user communicating via the VLC link. In this paper, the RF and FSO connections are defined by the Nakagami-m and Malaga distribution respectively. The VLC link is based on geometrical modeling with intensity modulation (IM)/direct detection (DD). This paper analyzed the secrecy performance of the aforementioned system from a physical layer perspective. To do this, the secrecy outage probability (SOP) is derived and analyzed in closed form. The results are obtained by considering the different turbulence strengths and field of view (FOV) of VLC link. The outcomes are confirmed by the use of Monte Carlo simulations. The influence of system and channel characteristics on SOP performance is explored and addressed.

articleTitle: DiaMOS Plant Leaves Disease Classification using Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The consequences of climate change have increased during the past several years. This climate influences each stage of plant production, and farmers are being forced to modify the plantation and advance their crop management techniques utilizing recent technology built on data analytics. Many plant diseases manifest themselves in the leaves. Therefore, successful disease diagnosis requires a thorough understanding of the condition of plants. To provide high-quality agricultural products, timely and precise disease detection and classification are crucial for smart and precision agriculture. In this study, images of the DiaMOS plant leaves dataset that was collected in the field of Sardegna, Italy is utilized to learn and classify plant disease using several fine-tuned z deep learning models like InceptionV3, EfficientNetB0, VGG-16, ResNet50, VGG-19. Here, the Deep learning models are trained to categorize the severity of plant disease and built a vision transformer for classification that achieves higher than the predefined models with an accuracy- 98.5% precision-97.1%, and F1 score – 97.83%.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependent Analysis of ZnO QDs Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Zinc Oxide (ZnO), a prominent II-VI group metal oxide semiconductor, has emerged as a potential contender for UV detection, especially under elevated temperature conditions. While Silicon (Si) has been traditionally explored, its efficacy diminishes at higher temperatures, highlighting the need for alternatives. ZnO, endowed with a wide band gap, radiation hardness, and piezoelectric properties, holds significant promise. Further, the quantum dot (QD) form of ZnO introduces enhanced spectrum selectivity due to its unique confinement properties. This research centers on the capabilities of ZnO QDs for high-temperature UV photodetection, spanning a temperature range from 303.15 K to 433.15 K. ZnO QDs have been thoroughly characterized and evaluated, providing important insights into their potential for UV photodetection under high temperature circumstances.

articleTitle: SSADV-Hop: Node Localization Approach in WSNs using a SSA based DV-Hop Range Free Method
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work addresses the node localization issue in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) by employing swarm-based algorithms and a range-free methodology. Determining the sensor node locations is one of the challenging tasks while dealing with WSNs. Range-based and Range-free approaches are used for distance measurement between sensor nodes. Range-free methods are more straightforward and don’t require any extra hardware compared to Range-Based methods. The most popular DV(Distance Vector)-Hop range-free method is used for distance measurement. The Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) is utilized to locate the unknown nodes because of its more straightforward behavior. The PSODV-Hop and DV-Hop-based approaches of node localization in WSNs are compared with the proposed SSADV-Hop approach’s solution using MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Security Framework for Electronic Health Record in the Cloud Based on Public key Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the modern world, medical data is managed and stored online so that anybody can access it at any time. For maintaining medical records and sharing with other healthcare providers, the majority of hospitals already use EHR (Electronic Health Records) with cloud storage. Medical data confidentiality, authentication, integrity, and access control are just a few of the security and privacy challenges that have arisen as a result of the growth of healthcare technology and the shift to Cloud computing. In this article, a Medi-locker has been introduced to keep all of the patient’s medical records where Both patient and medical practitioners can access healthcare documents at any time, from any location. To maintain the confidentiality and improve the security of the medical data Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), which enables operations to be performed on data that has been encrypted without even decrypting it. The proposed scheme has a high resistance to brute-force attacks when it is compared to other cryptosystem.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based On-Cloud Accident Detection and Reverse Geocoding Equipped Reporting System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: An accident is one of the significant problems that not only take life but also creates a disturbing environment on the road that can often lead to traffic jams resulting in retarded vehicular movement over the road. In this work, we develop a system that uses a power-efficient microcontroller pre-soldered with two sensors - an accelerometer and a gyroscope, along with two Android applications built using Flutter and a cloud-based Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) to intercommunicate among themselves for accident detection and reporting instantly. Whether it is a disastrous rolling accident down the slope of a hilly road or simply a head-on accident on highways and expressways or even in reverse motion collision-based accident, it detects the accident over the BaaS and further reports the particulars of the accident like name of the victim, time of the accidemt, location of the accident and details of the vehicle to emergency contacts provided by the victim(s). The algorithm written in Typescript and running in a Nodejs environment on the cloud, can gather and decode data to find patterns to detect accidents. By experimenting with the microcontroller mounted over a miniaturized car and driven to different types of accidents, it came to our observation that our system can achieve accurate accident detection and instant reporting.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency Class-E Power Amplifier with Tuned Output Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A switch-mode power amplifier (PA), like the proposed class-E renders itself capable of achieving a theoretical power conversion efficiency (PE) of 100% by ensuring specific bias and switching conditions of the active device and presenting an idealized impedance at the drain of the active device [1] [2] [3]. The design presented satisfies the zero-voltage switching (ZVS) and zero derivative voltage switching (ZVDS) conditions which are fundamental to correct class-E PA operation. The output network performs a dual function of impedance transformation to a standard 50 ohm impedance and harmonic suppression for any power being transmitted at harmonic frequencies.

articleTitle: Automatic Crop Irrigation System using Internet of Things and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Excessive irrigation causes adverse effects on the physical, chemical, and biological properties of soil, resulting in a decrease in its fertility. Therefore, the appropriate selection of irrigation methods is very important. Among these, furrow irrigation is found to be the most suitable alternative because of its high efficiency and low water consumption. The present work deals with the design, development, and simulation studies of a low-cost, fully automated, crop-independent, IoT-based furrow irrigation system. The system is designed by placing an array of wireless sensor nodes to investigate an adequate quantity of furrow flow rate and optimize it as per the requirements using a cloud computing platform. The designed system is advantageous in terms of saving water, benefiting crops, and subsiding soil degradation. The moisture sensors were deployed in the crop field with the help of a signal conditioning circuit interfaced with a microcontroller-integrated Wi-Fi module (ESP8266-NodeMCU). The said module was also connected to a solenoid valve to regulate the inflow rate and the Thing Speak cloud computing platform. The WinSRFR 5.1.1 simulation tool was used to estimate the adequate amount of flow rate suitable for the crop and soil type. The cloud platform was used to acquire, store, and process data to forecast the ideal soil moisture levels for future crop development and soil health. The studies were carried out at a depth of 100 mm and by varying furrow length (50 to 150 m) in steps of 50m for four different soil types, namely coarse sand soil, sandy loam soil, silt loam soil, and black cotton-plowed soil, which are commonly observed in India. The simulation work in this paper indicates the effectiveness of this system that how we can reduce the water loss by low-cost, fully automated, crop-independent, IoT-based furrow irrigation system.

articleTitle: LoRaWAN based Environmental Monitoring for Smart Campus
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has made it possible to implement creative methods to enhance the sustainability, security, and efficiency of modern campuses. In this paper, we describe the environment monitoring system for smart campuses based on LoRaWAN. The suggested system makes use of the Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) capabilities of LoRaWAN to provide an affordable and scalable way to collect real-time data from multiple sensors connected to LoRa shields installed across the campus. These sensors will monitor the temperature and humidity in the environment. The LoRa shield wirelessly transmits data to a central LoRaWAN gateway, which can be configured on a cloud server, such as The Things Network (TTN) platform, for data access. ThingSpeak has been utilized for better data visualization.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Enhanced Handwritten Devanagari Character Recognition using Image Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research work aims to improve the accuracy in identifying characters written in the Devanagari script, which is extensively used in a number of South Asian languages, including Hindi, Sanskrit, and Nepali, etc. The proposed work includes the development of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for enhanced handwritten Devanagari character recognition, with an emphasis on enhancing model performance through data augmentation. Data augmentation involves a set of techniques that increase the size of the dataset and balance classes by applying various transformations, aiding model prediction, and overfitting. Results are also analyzed on the basis of different performance measures like accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score. The proposed CNN model provides high accuracy with batch normalization and dropout layers, improving model training and generalization.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction using Transformers: A Federated Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: An increasingly popular renewable energy source is wind power. It aids in overcoming the depletion of non-renewable energy sources and moves a nation closer to sustainable growth. The main challenge of supply and demand optimization in the smart grid is resolved with the aid of wind power prediction, which also lowers operational costs and increases the dependability of the systems. But wind power is mainly distinguished by fluctuations and randomness making it difficult to predict. There are also concerns of privacy due to heavy commercial competition. In this paper, transformers are used for wind power prediction. To overcome the privacy issue, federated learning approach is used to train the transformers. The transformer model trained using federated learning approach is providing the best performance with an RMSE value of 201.25.

articleTitle: Real-Time Crowd-Counting and Management in Sacred places using Computer Vision & ESP32 cameras
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Flexible solution for real-time crowd counting and control in holy places that provides flexibility of an ESP32 camera and the accuracy of YOLOv8 object detection framework. It is designed to ensure crowd safety and prevent potential stampedes in dynamically changing religious environment. ESP32 cameras strategically placed throughout the sanctuary, recording live video feeds, allowing easy relocation based on changing audience dynamics on different days or times of the week. These video streams are forwarded to a central server for efficient processing. The server preprocesses and uses the YOLOv8 model to accurately count the number of people in each area. The system includes actuators such as automatic motorized door controls and information LCD screens to direct visitors to less crowded areas. The proposed solution addresses the unique challenges facing holy places by offering a comprehensive and customizable approach to crowd counting and management, thereby improving the safety and sanctity of religious settings. The precision obtained when compared to state-of-the-art systems was 68.9%

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of UAV Communication System in the Vicinity of Multiple Interferers
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: There is an increasing interest in the research arena for analyzing the performance of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, main objective during the design is to include all the important parameters in the study. The present research work analyzes the ground-to-UAV uplink communication system in the vicinity of multiple interfering UAVs. To make the system more accurate, 3-D coordinate representation of all the UAVs has been considered. Also, small-scale fading has been modeled using the square Gamma random variates. We derive an expression for the probability density function (PDF) for the sum of squared and scaled Gamma random variables. Using the derived expression, a closed-form expression of the outage probability has been presented. The derived results are accurate and have been simulated to study the impact of neighboring interfering UAV on the system.

articleTitle: Metal Strip Layer Approach to Enhance the DC Characteristics and Analog/RF Performance of a Dual Material Control Gate TFET
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach to enhance the electrical characteristics of the dual material control gate tunnel field effect transistor (DMCG-TFET) by introducing metal strips (referred to as MS) into the oxide layer at the source-channel (S-C) region are presented. This modification has led to the creation of a new device called the dual material control gate metal-strip tunnel FET (DMCG-MS-TFET). Furthermore, we have incorporated an optimization step in our work to select a suitable work function for the metal strip. The simulation results using Silvaco ATLAS software have demonstrated significant improvements in the ON-state current $\left(I_{O N}=\mathbf{1. 8 6} \times \mathbf{1 0}^{-6}\right.$ A), average subthreshold slope $\left(S S_{A v g}\right.$) of approximately 56.5 $\mathrm{mV} /$ decade, switching ratio $\left(I_{O N} / I_{O F F}\right)$ of $4.73 \times 10^{10}$, suppression of ambipolar current, transconductance value of $\left(g_{m}=\right.$ $1.04 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~S}$), and improvements in analog/RF figure of merit (FOMs). The simulation results show that the proposed device has a lot of potential for use in future high-frequency and analog circuits, especially when low gate voltages are needed for low-power and radio-frequency circuits.

articleTitle: Data Analytics Technique of Different IP Address Utilized for Cloud Services
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The utilization of different IP addresses for cloud services has become a critical aspect of modern data analytics. As cloud computing continues to revolutionize the way organizations store, process, and manage data, the need to optimize data analytics techniques for diverse IP address utilization has grown exponentially. This research delves into the various methods and strategies employed to effectively harness the power of multiple IP addresses in the cloud environment. The abstracted study begins by exploring the significance of IP addresses in cloud services and how their dynamic allocation can impact data analysis. It delves into the challenges faced by data analysts in handling varying IP addresses, such as security concerns, network complexities, and data consistency. Subsequently, the research highlights innovative techniques and tools designed to efficiently manage and analyze data from different IP sources. These include load balancing algorithms, virtual IP mapping, and geo-distributed data processing. Moreover, the research assesses the benefits and limitations of each approach, considering factors like performance, scalability, and cost-effectiveness. It also examines real-world case studies and success stories of companies that have leveraged these techniques to gain a competitive edge in the cloud-based data analytics landscape. In conclusion, the study advocates for the adoption of optimized data analytics techniques that incorporate diverse IP address utilization to maximize the potential of cloud services and facilitate data-driven decision-making in modern enterprises.

articleTitle: An Interactive and Economical Embedded Braille Machine for the Visually Challenged People
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper addresses the pressing global issue of visual impairment by introducing an interactive Braille device designed to enhance the quality of life for visually impaired individuals. The alarming statistic of a person going blind every five seconds underscores the urgency of providing effective solutions. Visually impaired individuals encounter substantial challenges, ranging from limited access to information and educational resources to obstacles in daily life, resulting in very low Braille literary rates [1]–[2]. Tragically, social isolation and discrimination have terrible consequences, with 40% of blind children not surviving past the age of five. Our proposed device facilitates Braille reading and writing with audio support, offering features like document reading, Braille-to-text conversion, and bilingual language support. Unlike traditional piezo-electric-based displays that consume excessive power for character generation through dynamic slot actuation, the solenoid-based approach significantly reduces power consumption while offering mechanical reliability and portability for users. Crucially, the device provides an affordable and economical solution to these challenges.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement in Electric Vehicle Charging Station using PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Bidirectional converters control for electric vehicles plays an important part in the Vehicle to grid (V2G) system. With the help of Electric vehicles, we can limit the use of natural resources and it also reduces pollution. Also, with increase in population there is huge demand of electricity due to which natural resources are getting depleted day by day, with this technology we can overcome this problem as battery contains huge amount of power, so by supplying it back to the grid or wherever we want to we can eventually contribute in controlling the depletion of natural resources as well as mitigating the pollution. To overcome this problem electrical vehicles are one of the most prominent technologies which has come to light. There are certain problems in these charging stations which can reduce the life of the batteries of electric vehicles. EVs problem are mainly concerns with power quality issues like harmonics, voltages imbalance, noises etc. It takes a battery as energy storage with a bidirectional buck-boost converter to regulate charging and discharging mode. The charging and discharging mechanism for a battery that stores electricity is managed by a charge controller. The controller in a bidirectional charger is essential for managing power flow, ensuring safety, facilitating communication with external systems, and optimizing the overall performance of the charging system. Alternately, control of bidirectional converter using PI controller. To counter this issue so that the battery life can be increased, and the other power quality issue also be mitigated.

articleTitle: A Trust-based Framework for the Detection and Avoidance of Blackhole Nodes in Opportunistic Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: An Opportunistic Network (OppNet), as opposed to a ubiquitous centralized network, relies on sporadic and opportunistic encounters between nodes to facilitate communication. The uncertainty about the node’s nature presents challenges when nodes with malicious intents are present in the network. One category of malicious nodes includes blackhole nodes, which receive messages but drop them intentionally. In this paper, we introduce a novel trust function designed to detect blackhole nodes within the network. Our function has been widely tested and simulated to validate and increase the efficacy of transmission of messages in the network. We have performed a comparative analysis with various protocols (PROPHET, Epidemic and Spray And Wait) on several parameters such as Delivery Ratio, Overhead Ratio and Number of Messages dropped. The results demonstrate that our trust function is able to correctly detect and avoid blackhole nodes. We observed significant improvement in delivery ratio in Epidemic Routing (47%), Prophet (41%), and Spray And Wait Routing (17%) protocols when adjusting blackhole nodes while keeping the total network nodes constant.

articleTitle: Optical Analysis of TiO2 and MoO3 based Optoelectronic Devices using Solcore
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this work, we have presented the optical analysis of multilayer optoelectronic devices. The devices are illuminated from the substrate side to achieve a 100% illumination area. A Solcore (python-based library) based study has been presented to predict the optical behavior of the devices. A comparative study has been presented considering ITO/TiO$_{2} /$CdSe or PbSe/MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based devices. The introduction of different layers is observed for the variation in effective absorption. The backscattering effect of the different electrodes is also observed to improve the optical absorption of the device.

articleTitle: ECG Dimensionality Reduction using PCA and Feature Abstraction Expending ICA Built with Power Spectral Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Electrocardiography, which is more often referred to as an electrocardiogram, is a way of monitoring the electrical activity of the heart over a period of time using electrodes that are put on the skin. These electrodes are able to pick up on the minute electrical changes in the skin that occur as a direct consequence of the electrophysiological pattern of depolarization and repolarization that occurs in the heart muscle with each beating. It is typically done to detect heart problems. The primary focus of this study is on extracting features from ECG wave data using Independent Component Analysis and Principal Component Analysis, both of which were developed with the help of a non-parametric power spectral estimation method. In a real-time setting, doctors establish diagnoses using criteria based on a minimal set of features extracted from an electrocardiogram. Parameters like signal amplitudes, distances, slopes, and morphology fall within this category. The primary goal of feature extraction is the real-time extraction of ECG signal components, which provides the necessary data for specialists or doctors to do additional analysis. Feature Extraction is largely accountable for reducing the effort and time needed to effectively describe large data sets. When analyzing complicated data, the amount of variables that must be taken into consideration in order to complete the analysis is often the biggest bottleneck. Analyses performed on large datasets place additional demands on the system's memory and processing power. Dimensionality reduction primarily entails defining a system with fewer, more manageable variables through the use of vector-based reduction techniques. Features are extracted from the reduced variables that can be used in the processing. Therefore, PCA is used for dimensionality reduction and ICA constructed with non-parametric power spectral estimation is used for feature extraction to accomplish classification in this work.

articleTitle: Cluster-Head Selection Protocol for Improving the Network Lifetime of Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Prolonged network operations are crucial for any Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) based applications such as health care, military, industrial, etc. The fixed energy and the restrained communication range of the sensor nodes (SNs) make it challenging to achieve a longer life of network operations. Generally, the data collection and direct message transmissions to the base station (BS) consume most of the SNs’ energy resulting in a shorter network lifetime. Reduction in the energy expended on these data transmissions leads to an improvement in the WSNs’ network lifetime. Clustering approaches are employed to mitigate this issue. The cluster head (CH) in each cluster collects the data from the SNs and forwards it to the BS. Proper CH node selection is vital in achieving enhanced network lifetime. Therefore, in this work, a new clustering technique is proposed that probabilistically selects the best CHs for each cluster by considering the residual energy of each SN. The suggested technique has been compared with the existing LEACH scheme and the experimental outcomes show the suggested technique has improved the network lifetime by an average of 8.32% and 14.23% in terms of the first and the last node dead respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Pattern for Searching Motion Vector in Interframe Coding
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Interframe coding is a highly effective method for compressing video data, especially when consecutive frames exhibit strong visual similarities or when motion follows predictable patterns, facilitated by motion estimation. This technique achieves significant compression while preserving the perceived video quality. Prominent video codecs that utilize interframe compression include H.264, H.265 (High Efficiency Video Coding), and others. In this research paper, an innovative pattern has introduced to improve rapid block motion estimation used in inter frame coding. When compared to previously employed patterns in block motion estimation, our newly proposed pattern excels in identifying motion vectors and requires fewer search points. It surpasses established methods, particularly in motion vector search tasks. This study highlights how the suggested pattern reduces the number of required search points compared to previous techniques, ultimately enhancing the accuracy of motion vector estimation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of UWB Fractal Array Antenna for 5G and Millimeter Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a fractal-inspired Array antenna designed for 5G millimeter-wave applications, aiming to meet the demands of the modern scenario for high-gain, compact, and low-profile antennas capable of high data rate communication with multiple devices. The antenna is developed over an FR-4 substrate with dimensions of $39.2\times 39.2\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}^{2}$. By incorporating the Sierpinski carpet fractal, the antenna exhibits ultra-wideband behavior with multiple notches, making it highly versatile for various wireless communication applications. Operating within the 24-40 GHz frequency range, the proposed antenna achieves a peak gain of 4.8 dBi and a front-to-back ratio of 10.5 dB. It demonstrates multiple resonant notches over wide bands, showing peak return loss values of 29, 30, 33, and 46.21 dB at 28.68, 29.68, 33.21, and 38.62 GHz, respectively. Implementing CST Studio Suite 2022 and validation with a Vector Network Analyzer has verified the antenna’s performance. The versatile nature of this antenna makes it suitable for applications in n-257, n-258, n-259, n-260, and n-261 bands, meeting the requirements of modern wireless communication scenarios with high efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: IOT Based Soldier Tracking and Health Indication System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an IoT-based soldier tracking and health indication (STHI) system utilizing the Arduino Uno microcontroller integrated with vital sensing and communication modules. The system aims to monitor and provide real-time updates on a soldier’s location, health parameters, and physical condition, enabling timely intervention and support. The proposed system incorporates various sensors including SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>sensor to measure blood oxygen saturation levels and heart rate, a temperature sensor to monitor body temperature, a vibration sensor to detect falls or physical impacts, a GPS module for precise location tracking, and a GSM module for seamless communication. Through the integration of wireless communication technologies, the system establishes a robust communication link between soldiers and the military command center. The collected data is transmitted wirelessly to the command center, where it is analyzed and evaluated by the experts. A Help button is added to the system for sending distress messages in case of emergency with location coordinates to the command center. Tracking of soldier locations enables efficient deployment of resources during critical situations, while monitoring of health parameters provides early warning signs for potential health issues.

articleTitle: Effect of Air Pollution on OFDM based RoFSO Transmission for Different Dust Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The proposed communication model using OFDM based radio over free space optical (RoFSO) system with WDM multiplexing is implemented. Two different 20Gbps - 60GHz data streams are transmitted at optical carriers of 193.1 THz and 193.3 THz frequency through single channel FSO link. The FSO link performance is analyzed for various dust conditions. The effect of channel attenuation due to size of suspended dust concentration in terms of particulate matter i.e. PM10 and PM2.5 is analyzed. The effect of various atmospheric turbulence conditions under light dust conditions is also considered in the analysis. Eye diagram pattern is observed under different dust conditions and corresponding bit error rate and Q-factor is measured. At detector output, SNR is measured by using spectrum analyzer. Also, electric constellation is observed for PM 10 and PM 2.5 under various dust conditions using constellation visualizer. The channel attenuation due to the combined effect of various dust pollutants and atmospheric turbulence conditions on FSO link is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Optimum Feature Selection for the Analysis of Effects of Electroencephalography on Applied Pressure Physiotherapy
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Applied Pressure Physiotherapy (APP) approaches have been widely acknowledged as helpful in treating a wide range of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders. However, the impact of these methods on mental performance has only been partially explored. The research being conducted will provide an exploratory examination of how APP affects EEG spectral patterns, which may help researchers better understand the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms that contribute to the therapeutic benefits of such therapies. Improved classifier performance is possible thanks to feature selection’s potential to lessen the impact of noise in the data, overtraining, storage requirements, and computing complexity. These objectives have been met through the application of various feature selection techniques. A novel hybrid feature selection strategy is proposed in this research. Performance is measured using a support vector machine classifier; features are extracted using a Filter-Bank similar spatial resolution pattern; and an ideal feature subset is found and generated using the grey wolf optimization algorithm. The preliminary findings demonstrate that the suggested methods outcompete the cutting-edge methods even with limited training data.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Modulation Scheme Classification in RF Signals within Cognitive Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Dynamic Spectrum Access (DSA) plays a crucial role in cognitive radio (CR) by effectively utilizing unused spectrum and meeting the escalating traffic demands of advanced cellular networks like 5G and beyond. A significant focus in recent years has been on employing Deep Learning (DL) architectures for Radio Frequency (RF) signal classification in CR-based applications. This paper presents the development of a DL-based framework using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture to classify various modulation schemes, including Continuous-phase frequency-shift keying (CPFSK), Gaussian Frequency Shift Keying(GFSK), 64 quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM), Binary Phase-shift keying (BPSK), 16QAM, Gaussian Minimum Shift Keying (GMSK), QPSK of a signal received from the base stations in Global System for Mobile communication (GSM) network. The performance evaluation of the proposed CNN architecture will be conducted using real-time GSM signals obtained from nearby base stations. The performance analysis of each network architecture is presented and analyzed.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Angle Effect of L-Shaped Beam Branches on the Performance of Multi-Resonant Piezoelectric Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent years, the continuous development in nonlinear piezoelectric energy harvesting (PEH) devices has increased the efficiency of self powered electronic devices by harvesting energy from more than one resonant frequency. In literature, various techniques and structures of non-linear PEH devices have been proposed. This paper is mainly considered L-shaped and horizontal beam branches based nonlinear PEH device for study purposes. This device is associated with the advantages of low acceleration (0.2g) operating condition and more than one resonant peaks below 9 Hz frequency range. In presented paper, the behaviour of nonlinear PEH device is examined corresponding to the changes in positioning angles of perpendicular part of L-shaped beams using COMSOL Multiphysics software. From this simulation study, it has been observed that by keeping 90 degree angle between perpendicular and horizontal parts of L-shaped branches, the multi-resonant device resonates at 6.4 Hz, 6.9 Hz and 7.4 Hz resonant frequencies with improved value of voltage (27.8 V, 9.9 V, 23.6 V) and power response (6.4 Hz, 6.9 Hz, 7.4 Hz).

articleTitle: Real Time Cloud-Based Weather Monitoring System using NodeMCU
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Cloud-based real-time weather monitoring systems are emerging Internet of Things (IoT) technologies that enable the collection, storage, and remote access of weather parameters. The system uses IoT devices and a cloud platform to collect and store constant weather data for small areas, including: B. Temperature, humidity, rain, pressure. The collected information is transmitted in real-time on the internet to a cloud servers on thingSpeak.com, making the data easily accessible and visualized through the website interface. The purpose of this system is to provide an advanced weather monitoring solution leveraging IoT technology and provide easy access to a wide range of real-time weather data. The system integrates IoT devices such as sensors and uses the NodeMCU platform to send the collected data to cloud servers. It uses cloud computing to store and process data efficiently and allows users to access weather information remotely. The data can be visualized and analysed through a user-friendly website interface, facilitating monitoring and analysis of weather conditions in specific regions. Integrating IoT and cloud computing into a real-time weather monitoring system offers several advantages. First, it enables the collection of 80% accurate and up-to-date weather data, facilitating better decision making in many sectors such as agriculture, transportation and disaster management. Second, cloud-based approach ensures scalability and flexibility when dealing with large amounts of data. Additionally, the system’s architecture facilitates expansion and integration with other IoT devices and services, enhancing its capabilities for future applications.

articleTitle: Lint, CDC and RDC analysis for PCIe subsystem using VC_Spyglass
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: this project focuses on addressing critical Lint, CDC, and RDC challenges in chip design Where different parts of the system operate on signals with varying clock frequencies. To ensure the proper synchronization and handling of these signals and mitigate potential timing violations and functional failures, Lint, CDC, and RDC analyses are done. Spyglass is a widely used tool for carrying out this analysis. The study involves a comprehensive analysis, debugging, and modification of design related to missing or incorrect declarations, uninitialized variables, unreachable code, and coding guideline violations. Additionally, the project extensively examines CDC issues, such as metastability and data corruption risks, and leverages Spyglass to identify problems like inadequate synchronization techniques, missing synchronization paths, and violations of CDC guidelines. SoC designs have a variety of reset sources, including hardware resets, software resets, watchdog timer resets, debug resets, and power-on resets.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Assessment of a Si/GaSb-PC-TFET for Label-Free Bio-Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a Si/GaSb-polarity control tunnel field effect transistor (Si/GaSb-PC-TFET) is proposed as a label-free biosensor. To enhance the sensing performance of the proposed biosensor, a narrow band-gap heteromaterial named GaSb is employed in the source region. The dielectric constant $(k)$ and charge density ($\mathrm{N}_{\text {bio }}$) of various biomolecules are utilized for assessing their presence via the proposed Si/GaSb-PC-TFET-based biosensor. In the proposed work, we considered the biomolecules with dielectric constants $(k)$ from 1 to 12 and charge densities ranging from $\pm 1 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{C.cm}^{-2}$ to $\pm 1 \times 10^{12} \mathrm{C.cm}^{-2}$ with a fixed k-value. The sensing efficiency of the proposed biosensor has been determined in terms of drain current ($\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{DS}}$), and the maximum $\mathrm {I_{D S}}$ sensitivity is obtained as $1.11 \times 10^{13}$ for neutra $(k=12)$ and $1.28 \times 10^{13}$ for negatively charged $(N_{\text {bio }}=-1 \times 10^{12}$ C. $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}, k=12$) biomolecules. Furthermore, the sensitivity of the proposed Si/GASb-PC-TFET biosensor has also been investigated by employing different partially filled nano-cavities.

articleTitle: Efficient Approximate 8-Bit Binary Parallel Subtractor Circuit: Design, Analysis, and Application in Negative Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the field of image processing and computer vision, negative imaging is vital for applications like medical imaging, art, and data enhancement. This paper introduces an efficient approach for negative image creation using an approximate 8-bit binary parallel subtractor (ABPS) circuit. The ABPS circuit reduces area usage by 33% and significantly cuts delay by 68.4% compared to conventional subtractor. The ABPS circuit balances precision and speed, making it ideal for tasks where small errors are acceptable. The efficacy of ABPS is demonstrated through its successful application in generating negative images, underscoring its performance.

articleTitle: Investigation of CeO₂/rGO Nanocomposites as Diesel Additives to Enhance Engine Performance and Reduce Exhaust Emissions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this study, Cerium Oxide nanoparticles (CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NPs) and CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-rGO (Cerium oxide + reduced graphene oxide) nanocomposites are used to improve performance and reduce harmful gas emissions in diesel fuel. Cerium oxide nanoparticles and CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-rGO nanocomposites have been developed by one-pot hydrothermal process at different temperatures, viz. 100 °C, 300 °C, and 500 °C in the presence of cetyltrimethylammonium bromide and aqueous ammonia. A few exhaust parameters were taken into consideration, including carbon monoxide (CO), particulate matter (PM), nitrogen oxide (NOx), unburned hydrocarbons (UHC), break thermal efficiency (BTE), and break specific fuel consumption (BSFC). The results showed that CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-rGO500 nanocomposites at 30 ppm reduce harmful emissions while increasing engine efficiency. This study further confirms the role of CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-rGO based nanocomposites as potential catalysts owing to their inimitable physiochemical properties.

articleTitle: A Deep Dive into Accurate Garbage Classification Using Transfer Learning Techniques for Environmental Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Accurate garbage classification is a pillar in modern waste management systems, carrying profound implications for sustainability and environmental impact reduction. This study represents a significant leap forward in the domain of garbage classification, driven by the application of state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms enhanced by transfer learning methodologies.
