We employ a comprehensive garbage classification dataset, encompassing a diverse array of waste categories including plastics, paper, glass, and organic materials, to explore the potential of selecting pre-trained deep learning architectures. Models such as ResNet-50, DenseNet-161, InceptionV3, and EfficientNet-B7 are employed and subjected to thorough evaluation for their classification capabilities. Leveraging transfer learning to enhance their performance, we incorporate logistic regression as a multi-class classifier. Our findings reveal remarkable test accuracies for these models. ResNet-50 shines with a notable accuracy of 94.70%, closely followed by DenseNet-161 at 93.25%. InceptionV3 maintains competitive performance with an accuracy of 92.54%, while EfficientNet-B7 impresses with a significant test accuracy of 93.75%. These results collectively underscore the exceptional performance of these models in automating waste classification tasks, showing the effectiveness of deep learning coupled with transfer learning and logistic regression methodologies. Such advancements hold the potential to revolutionize waste management practices, fostering sustainability and responsible waste handling.

articleTitle: Design a UWB Antenna with Band Notch Characteristics for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a rectangular shape ultra-wideband (UWB) two elements multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna. The proposed antenna design is simulated and verified through two software Ansys HFSS and CST Studio Suite. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna offers an impedance bandwidth of 111.4% from 3.3 GHz to 11.6 GHz. To mitigate the effect of WLAN (5.15 – 5.875 GHz) a U-shaped slot is etched at the center of the radiator. Further, in order to enhance the isolation a stub (decoupler) is inserted between MIMO elements. It is found that isolation is significantly improved through the entire frequency band. The MIMO parameters like ECC, DG, MEG, and CCL are also analyzed and all are found within acceptable limits. Further, an electrical equivalent circuit of the proposed antenna is designed using ADS software.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Enabled Dual-hop NOMA Relaying System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work presents a dual hop system where a source communicates with multiple users via a Decode and Forward (DF) relay in between. The Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technique is applied at the user terminals for signal detection. This paper introduces the Deep Learning (DL) technique which is replacing the traditional Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) technique of signal detection at the user terminal. The major challenges which signal suffers are channel distortion and multiuser signal superposition. The DL method combines the channel estimation and signal recovery process for the affected signal. The system model is designed for Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) system. As per the results, the DL shows improved signal detection in comparison to SIC method for NOMA technique. The Deep Neural Network (DNN) algorithm is applied to retrieve the signal. Therefore, the novel approach of MIMO-DL-NOMA for dual-hop system is a promising approach to resolve issues faced by SIC method.

articleTitle: Real-Time Image Super-Resolution using Drone through GFPGAN and Nvidia Jetson Nano
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Blind facial restoration generally uses facial priors, including a reference or a facial geometrical prior, to restore accurate and realistic details. The absence of severely low-quality inputs and the lack of high-quality references, however, significantly restrict its relevance to real-world situations. This work shows a GFPGAN model for blind face restoration that utilizes the rich and varied priors present in a pre-trained face GAN to enhance the quality and perspective of images captured by a drone in real-time. Implementing this model on an edge AI device illustrates the harmonious combination of realism and fidelity in face restoration. This is achieved by evaluating its performance on different images captured from various angles and distances. For processing on edge AI devices, the suggested system uses an Nvidia Jetson Nano, an affordable but powerful single-board computer. We present the results of a feasibility study demonstrating the capacity of GFPGAN to improve the caliber of real-time drone photography.

articleTitle: An Angle Independent Cross Arrow Shaped Resistor Loaded Metamaterial Absorber for Wideband EMC/EMI Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper put forward design and investigation of a wideband angle-stable microwave absorber for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC)/ electromagnetic interference (EMI) applications for entire complete C - and X bands. The proposed unit-cell composed of four cross arrow shaped resonators joined via circular ring, which encloses slotted circular patch. Four lumped resistors are mounted on the shaft of each arrow to enhance the ohmic power dissipation, which leads to wideband absorption performance. The investigations conducted in this work demonstrate that the intended absorber is capable to provide larger than 90% absorptivity from 3.83 to $12.03 \mathrm{GHz}(8.2 \mathrm{GHz} \approx 103.4 \%)$. Also, the peak absorptivity of 99.63% and 99.34% is attained at 4.65 GHz and 10.90GHz, respectively. The miniaturized cell size and thickness of the absorber is only $0.169 \lambda_{L}$ and $0.082 \lambda_{L}$, respectively ($\lambda_{L}$ is determined at lowest absorption frequency). Moreover, the polarization conversion ratio has been calculated from co- and cross-polarized reflection coefficients to validate that the proposed unit-cell is not exhibiting polarization conversion characteristics and working as an absorber. The polarization insensitive behavior has been achieved due to 90° rotational symmetry of the suggested absorber structure. In addition, it offers stable absorption performance against incident angle variations up to 45° for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarized waves.

articleTitle: Instantaneous Fundamental Frequency Estimation based on FBSE-FAWT
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Instantaneous fundamental frequency (IFF) estimation plays an important role in speech processing. This paper proposes a method for estimating a speech signal’s IFF based on the Fourier-Bessel series expansion-based flexible analytic wavelet transform (FBSE-FAWT). The proposed method uses an FBSE- FAWT-based filter bank to decompose the signals into subbands. Components corresponding to the fundamental frequency (FF) can be present in more than one subband. Therefore, a set of subbands are selected whose mean frequency is found to be in the range of 50-500 Hz. In each subband, there may be components separated in the time domain. So for the separation of these components, a new method for time-domain segmentation (TDS) using the Teager-Kaiser energy operator (TKEO) is introduced. Then Hilbert transform separation algorithm (HTSA) based processing is performed on these separated components to obtain the IFF of the speech signal. As a post-processing step, cubic spline interpolation is performed to get accurate IFF. To validate the proposed method, the Keele database is used and the results are compared with the traditional methods. Experimentally it is proved that the IFF estimation method based on FBSE- FAWT is working better and improves the time-resolution of IFF estimation.

articleTitle: CFD Algorithms for Magnesium Based Implant System for Smooth Pursuit Eye Movements
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a degenerative retinal disease that is a leading cause of blindness in individuals aged 50 and above. Macular hole degeneration is a prevalent cause of blindness in patients and is typically managed through the administration of anti-VEGF drugs. A magnesium-based implant device is used in the treatment of AMD to administer medication, effectively reducing the need for injections. The development of drug delivery devices that improve treatment outcomes is crucial, and magnesium shows promise as a potential substance for this purpose. Magnesium plays a crucial role in the functioning of the eyes. Magnesium exhibits advantageous properties such as low corrosion resistance, biodegradability, and biocompatibility. This study aims to investigate the impact of ocular fluid dynamics on an implant device within the vitreous humor. The study investigated the impact of various smooth pursuit eye movement periods on the flow-induced total pressure response on the external surfaces of the device. The smooth pursuit eye movements at frequencies of $1 \mathrm{~Hz}, 2 \mathrm{~Hz}$, and $3 \mathrm{~Hz}$ were simulated using computational fluid dynamics (CFD), without any rest intervals. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) was employed to analyze the pressure distribution on a magnesium-based device designed for smooth pursuit eye movements within the ocular vitreous chamber. This study analyzed the impact of fluid-induced vitreous splashing on the intravitreous administration of drug delivery medications.

articleTitle: Statistical Physical Model for Rise and Fall Time Analysis of DMNC System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Nano communication is having a subset class of Diffusion Molecular Communication (DMC) which is the most popular and evolving. Time channel is a common channel model in diffusive MNC. Diffusion of Molecules in DMC results in prediction of performance metrics and count of diffused molecules as well. It is most important to mention that rise time as well as fall time both significantly contribute to overall transmission and reception time duration. DMC has great applicability in a spherical shaped environment in contrast to a rectangular-shaped environment. Human body has many entities which such as the kidney, stomach, lungs, and cells are sphere-shaped so they have great importance in DMC. Therefore, in this short Communication, rise time and fall time of the DMC system are analyzed by presenting close form expressions of each of them. The rising time value decreases and the fall time value increases with increasing transmitter and receiver distance. Numerical analysis shows a good match with the theory. Also the proposed work is beneficial for future nano networks applications that interface with biological processes in living things because of its close association with biological environment and viability at cellular networks.

articleTitle: An Array of Fibonacci Hexagon based Printed Radiators for Vehicular Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article presents a concept for using a printed array of hexagonal radiators in vehicle-to-vehicle applications. The IEEE 802.11p standard designates the frequency range of 5.85 to 5.925 GHz for dedicated short-range communication specifically tailored for vehicle applications. The singular radiator has been developed from regular hexagonal structures based on the Fibonacci sequence. The suggested construction has five hexagons, each with a length scaled down by a factor of 0.625. To provide connectivity between the hexagons, a vertical slit has been introduced, followed by the addition of a horizontal slit on the acquired structure. The Wilkinson power divider is employed in the configuration of the feed network of an array in order to achieve a substantial level of isolation. Implementing antennas in CST Microwave Studio entails using a single-layer printed circuit board (PCB) composed of FR-4 laminate material with a relative permittivity of 4.40. The antenna and the array have gains of 6.96 and 10.20 dBi, respectively, and possess a bandwidth coverage that exceeds 100%. Both antennas demonstrate a minimal level of cross-polarization in the principal beam direction. Both antennas have notable radiation efficiency and acceptable aperture efficiency, respectively. Due to its minimal correction factor values, the antenna shows a reduced electromagnetic interference (EMI) and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) effect. Both antennas are suitable choices for applications in vehicles.

articleTitle: Electrical Noise Analysis of Polarity Gate JLTFET
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper studies the noise characteristics of polarity gate junctionless TFET (PG JLTFET). The current simulation-based study aims to explore and evaluate the device’s frequency response to noise under different conditions. Some of the characteristics presented versus gate-to-source voltages are noise conductance, cross correlation, minimum noise figure, gate and drain autocorrelation, for device channel lengths of 15 nm, 20 nm, 25 nm, 30 nm, 35 nm, and 40 nm. The Silvaco two-dimensional device simulator ATLAS is used to perform the numerical simulation used as a validation tool. The noise characteristics of the junctionless device were found demonstrating excellent characteristics.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum Beam Antenna Systems for Wireless Communications – A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams, also known as vortex beams, have gained a significant attraction in the past decade. Their ability to offer an infinite number of modes (theoretically) opens doors to develop new high data-rate and secure communication system. In this paper, we present the general theory of OAM beams and give a brief overview of different techniques presented in the literature to achieve such beams with high order mode purity.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Dual-Hop NOMA based Communication System with Practical Constraints: Imperfect CSI, HWI and ISIC
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an asymmetric dualhop decode-and-forward relay-based Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) based communication system. The source-to-relay link is characterized by $\eta-\mu$ distribution, while the relay to end users is characterized by Rayleigh distribution. Further, we have incorporated hardware impairments (HWI), and channel state information (CSI) errors due to imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC), at the relay and end users. The mathematical framework for outage probability (OP) is being derived, and the analytical results are verified using Monte Carlo simulation results.

articleTitle: EXCCII-Based Precision Trans-Impedance-Mode Full Wave Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research study addresses newly designed trans-impedance mode full-wave rectifier using single current conveying active element extra-X second generation current conveyor. This rectifier design comprises one active element, two diodes and one resistor. The proposed design satisfies the integration technology requirement and also has low-voltage low-power feature. The proposed design is cascadable as a low input impedance terminal is used for the input current and low output impedance terminal is used to obtain the output voltage. The performance of the proposed rectifier is validated by standard tool PSPICE with 0.18 $\mu$m TSMC technology process parameters and all the simulated results are in accordance with theoretical concepts.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Study of Gaussian-Doped Channel in Stacked Gate Oxide MOS Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper examines the effect of Gaussian doping in the channel of a stacked gate oxide double-gate metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (SGO-DG-MOSFET), called the Gaussian-doped channel SGO-DG-MOSFET (GDC-SGO-DG-MOSFET). Using the technology computer-aided design (TCAD) tool, the simulation results of GDC-SGO-DG-MOSFET are compared with the uniform-doped channel SGO-DG-MOSFET (UDC-SGO-DG-MOSFET). The GDC-SGO-DG-MOSFET shows a reduction in the subthreshold leakage current.

articleTitle: Characterization of Radiation-Dependent Dual Channel AlGaN/GaN MOS-HEMT Based Dosimeter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: We have developed a Double channel MOSHEMT-based dosimeter. This paper presents the performance comparison between double channel HEMT based dosimeter and Double channel MOS-HEMT based dosimeter. Various Parameters such as Channel potential, Electric field, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf>-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf>, sensitivity, gate capacitance, and cut-off frequency have been analyzed for both the devices, and the double-channel MOSHEMT devices have good cutoff frequencies. These devices have excellent gain linearity and can function at higher input power and frequency levels. It has been found that the undoped barrier layer benefits Double Channel MOSHEMTs by increasing the drain current, widening the transconductance peak, and raising the threshold voltage. The presence of well-defined double-channel behaviour is well demonstrated by the formation of a double-hump structure in the dependency of and on gate bias. The effect of radiation dose $\left(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{t}}=2 \times 10^{12} \mathrm{~cm}^{-2}\right)$ has been studied. Maximum channel potential, Electric field, cut-off frequency and maximum current observed for the DC-MOS HEMT-based dosimeter device are 1.6059 V, 1.33E+05 V/cm, 1.89E+10, 0.069. Due to the extra oxide layer under the gate electrode, the DC-MOSHEMT-based dosimeter exhibits better results than the DC-HEMT-based dosimeter.

articleTitle: Design of Slotted Microstrip Antenna using Regression based Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Advancements in wireless communication technology have led to the development of compact and cost-effective microwave components. Among these components, microstrip patch antennas have gained popularity due to their versatility and ease of fabrication. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to design microstrip patch antennas using a combination of simulation, regression modeling, and prototype testing. The High-Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS) software is employed to digitally replicate antenna behavior and analyze the impact of slot dimensions on resonant frequency characteristics. A Gaussian Regression Process (GRP) model is developed to quantitatively correlate slot dimensions with resonant frequencies, facilitating efficient antenna design optimization. The proposed methodology is validated through the design, fabrication, and testing of prototype antennas, showcasing the accuracy and reliability of the developed regression model in predicting resonant frequencies based on varying slot dimensions. The study sheds light on the interdependence of antenna parameters and offers a streamlined approach to antenna design and prediction.

articleTitle: Computational Approaches to Optimizing Perovskite Solar Cell Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article represents a numerical simulation study for a hybrid Perovskite Solar Cell (PSC) with the following device stack structure Glass/ITO/PCBM/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Spiro-OMeTAD/Ag In this setup, PCBM serves as Electron transport layer (ETL),Spiro-OMeTAD is integrated as hole transport layer (HTL) and ITO is utilized as buffer layer. The research presents optimization and thorough systematic and comprehensive analysis performed on the hybrid PSC performance to examine the effects of variation in defect density, thickness, Bandgap, and acceptor density using the SCAPS-1D solar simulator software. The research reports maximum Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) of 28.99% for the hybrid PSC at defect density of $10^{14}~\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ and absorber layer thickness of $0.5 \mu\mathrm{~m}$ at 300 K.

articleTitle: WiCare: Accidental Fall Detection for Elderly Care Using Passive Wi-Fi Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Monitoring people’s activities serves various purposes, with accidental fall detection being a significant one. Existing technologies rely on wearable sensors, which are only sometimes practical, and privacy concerns surround camera-based solutions. This study introduces a non-invasive approach using passive Wi-Fi sensing to identify accidental falls, offering a way to detect people and devices in an area without additional sensors. The system employs deep neural networks to detect falls by analyzing Wi-Fi signal fluctuations caused by human movement. A substantial dataset of Wi-Fi signals collected during five activities (fall, pickup, sit down, stand up, and walk) in a smart home environment trains the deep learning model. Amplitude and phase, being the fundamental properties of a signal, are used as components in feature selection for our data set. We employed Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) and random forest algorithms to classify five activities. Our approach yielded a remarkable average accuracy of 98%, demonstrating its ability to identify and differentiate these activities based on WiFi signals precisely. This highlights the promising potential of WiFi sensing technology for practical applications in activity recognition and monitoring.

articleTitle: Road Detection from Remote Sensing Images using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Road detection from remote sensing images is vital in various applications, such as urban planning, transportation management, and navigation systems. In this work, we propose a methodology for road detection using deep learning architectures, including ResNet, U-Net, DenseNet, and MobileNet, with the DeepGlobe dataset. This work aims to accurately identify and delineate road pixels within remote sensing imagery. The objective is to compare the performance of different models and determine the most influential architecture for road detection. The proposed methodology involves data preprocessing, implementing the deep learning architectures, training the models, and evaluating their performance using metrics such as Intersection over Union (IoU), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio(PSNR). Experimental results show that ResNet achieves the highest accuracy, followed by U-Net, DenseNet, and MobileNet. Future work includes exploring multi-segmentation for detecting other features in remote sensing imagery, ensemble models, transfer learning, addressing occlusions and environmental variability, and efficient inference. By leveraging deep learning architectures and the DeepGlobe dataset, this work contributes to accurate road detection in remote sensing images, enabling improved urban and transportation planning decision-making.

articleTitle: Hardware Software Co-design of k-means Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The k-means clustering algorithm is a method that is frequently utilized for the purpose of grouping data points considering their similarity. Within the scope of this research, we investigate the viability of using a hardware-software co-design (HSC) strategy in order to speed up the k-means algorithm's execution. The studies are carried out using a Zedboard HSC platform based on Zynq 7000 architecture, which incorporates both processing system (PS) part implemented as set of instructions as software component and programmable logic (PL) part implemented on configurable FPGA fabric as hardware component using RTL code. In implementing k-means clustering algorithm, calculations of distance are carried out by PS and the results are communicated to PL, for performing the distance comparison & cluster reassignment. In order to reduce the resource utilization and the execution time, three different design configurations are being studied using HSC approach where the PL part follows different architectures. The results show comparison of execution speed, resource utilization and power when the different design architecture for the PL part are compared.

articleTitle: Magnetic Resonance Image Fusion using Bilateral Filter and PCA
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Three bands of magnetic resonance image—PD, T1 and T2—produce complimentary data about the human body portion being scanned. Medical image fusion combines complementary information of all three bands in the fused image with all relevant information needed by a physician to do medical analysis. This paper uses the edge-preserving bilateral filter and principal component analysis to combine complimentary data from PD, T1 and T2 bands of magnetic resonance images. Bilateral filter is used to decompose each of the three bands of magnetic resonance images into detail and approximation images. Detail image contains the high frequency information whereas approximation image contains the low frequency information. Principal component analysis and maximum absolute value are selected as the activity measure to fuse detail and approximation images. Then, the fused image is obtained by adding these fused detail and approximation images. Fusion metrics like Mutual information, Non-linear correlation information entropy, Structural similarity index measure, Gradient metric, Phase congruency metric and Human perception metric are used in this paper to compare the results of proposed method with image fusion using various pyramids, Wavelet and Curvelet Transforms.

Author Keywords: Structural similarity index measure. Gradient metric

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Peculiar Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor (PPPS) for Distinct Application
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In various industries where MEMS plays an important role in the field of sensors and its related applications like automotive, home appliance, biomedical and aerospace from which piezoresistive microcantilever sensor is a type mechanical microsensors which is under use since many years to understand different characteristic of a product. In this study it delves into the influence of discrete miniaturized piezoresistor shapes to check the performance of a pressure sensor tailored for precise measurements within the range of 1 to 10 bar. Utilizing CoventorWare simulation software, numerous piezoresistor configurations were systematically examined in which sensitivity of a product was tested with rectangular shape delivering 2.2 mV/bar, the U-shaped design offering 3 mV/bar, the Z-shaped configuration producing 7 mV/bar, and the S-shaped geometry leading with an impressive 13mV/bar sensitivity. On the basis of the simulation results conducted, S-shaped piezoresistor in particular stood out to be an optimal choice for applications necessitating high-precision pressure measurements and a comprehensive analysis underscores the adaptability of MEMS pressure sensors through piezoresistor shape customization.

articleTitle: Wavelet-based Alzheimer’s Disease Detection using Edge-Weighted Local Binary Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is a neurodegenerative syndrome that influences the people worldwide. As the disease progresses, it reduces the cognitive skills in individuals and makes them unable to perform their everyday tasks. In the proposed method a new feature extraction technique is proposed which captures the important biomarkers for early Alzheimer’s disease detection. In proposed technique Dual tree complex wavelet transform has been applied on 2-D MR slices to obtain six sub-band images. Further Edge weighted Local Binary Pattern has been applied on sub-band images to obtain edge prominent texture patterns. The dimensionality of these patterns is reduced by using Principal Component Analysis. The extracted features are then used for Alzheimer’s disease classification. Experimental results show that edge weighted Local Binary Pattern gives better classification results than normal Local Binary Pattern as edge weighted Local Binary Pattern provides the local gradient variation information. Different models have been compared in the paper to test the potential of proposed method. The proposed method has been implemented on Open Access Series of Imaging Studies dataset and remarkable results have been obtained in terms of accuracy of 94.2%, sensitivity of 96%, and specificity of 93%. The proposed method surpasses the performance of latest methods existing in literature for Alzheimer’s Disease detection.

articleTitle: Solar Powered IoT based Environment Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In an era marked by rapid evolution, the importance of effective environmental monitoring and precise weather prediction cannot be overstated. This paper introduces an independent robotic solution engineered to observe vital environmental metrics such as temperature, humidity, air quality, and levels of harmful gases. The robotic system is constructed around an Arduino, consolidating all sensors for monitoring environmental conditions. It seamlessly incorporates LoRa (Long-Range) technology for seamless real-time data transmission. Furthermore, random forest machine learning algorithms have been deployed to predict current weather conditions like sunny, cloudy, and rainy. Primary idea guiding the incorporation of renewable energy is to address the energy gap in rural areas without access to conventional power sources.

articleTitle: Drowsy Driving Detection System using Image Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The aim of this work is to develop a smart system that helps to prevent accidents caused by drowsy driving. Using the concept of machine learning and image processing, the status of the drivers can be monitored. If the driver starts to fall asleep, the system will notice and sound an alarm to wake them up. Even if the driver somehow feels tired, the system will recognize that too, and alert them. This system is connected to alarms both inside and outside the vehicle. It begins by capturing and extracting frames from a video. These frames are like snapshots taken from the video. Afterwards, the model processes each of these frames, finds the facial landmarks and calculates the Euclidean distance between the left, right, up and down of the eye and it will calculate the ratio between them. The ratio is to be compared with a threshold value and on the basis of this. If the calculation ratio is greater than the threshold, it indicates that the driver is fully conscious and normal and if the ratio holds within a certain range, then it implies the eyes are not open properly the driver is feeling drowsy and the system will alert the driver. While the ratio is less than or equal to the threshold value then the identified facial expression will indicate that the driver falls asleep, and then the system activates an alarm that sounds continuously for a certain time period. This proposed system can be used in trains, cars or any moving vehicles as a precaution or to avoid accidents due to drowsiness.

articleTitle: Detection of Counterfeit Currency Through SURF and Haar Cascade Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Counterfeit currency refers to unauthorized replica money produced with the intent to deceive. This issue has been on the rise in our country, with frequent reports of such fraudulent activities. The proliferation of technology, including computers, photocopiers, and scanners, has made counterfeiting currency notes increasingly accessible. Currently, we lack robust methods to distinguish between counterfeit and genuine currency. Addressing this pressing issue requires a range of solutions, including hardware-related techniques, chemical methods, and computer/software-based approaches. In this paper, we focus on software-based techniques and introduce four methods based on image processing principles for counterfeit currency detection: the brute force algorithm, HSV value detector, Haar cascade classifier, and security stripe detection using SURF.

articleTitle: Low Power Near-Threshold Schmitt-Trigger Driven 11T CNTFET SRAM Cell with Improved Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a Low power near-threshold $\left(V_{t h}\right)$ one sided Schmitt-trigger based 11T (ST 11T) carbon nanotube field-effect transistor (CNTFET) static random access memory (SRAM) cell. The proposed ST 11T shows less read delay $\left(T_{R A}\right)$, write delay $\left(T_{W A}\right)$, leakage power, and dynamic power consumption, respectively than other considered cells. It achieves better read & write stability, $I_{o n} / I_{o f f}$ ratio, respectively than other compared cells. The simulation utilizes Cadence Virtuoso with Stanford University $32 \mathrm{~nm}$ CNTFET model at a supply voltage $\left(V_{D D}\right)$ of 0.43 V.

articleTitle: 5G Network Slice Prediction using Hybrid Neural Network and Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: 5G networks are designed to be highly flexible and dynamic in order to meet the diverse needs and demands of users, such as faster internet, increased reliability, low latency and the ability to connect multiple devices. Network slicing, a prominent feature of 5G, enables flexibility by efficiently allocating resources through the creation of multiple virtual or logical connections on the same physical network structure. Recently, learning based models have found applications in various network slicing tasks such as predicting traffic, controlling slice admissions and efficiently allocating resources to make intelligent decisions. In this paper a novel hybrid model has been developed using the combination of a neural network and the random forest to predict the accurate network slice based upon network characteristics and user devices. The comparative performance analysis on a standard dataset shows that the proposed model performs better with an accuracy of 99.1% compared to other conventional deep learning algorithms in predicting the correct slice.

articleTitle: Software-Defined Networking’s Adaptive Load Optimisation Technique for Multimedia Applications with Multi-Controller Utilisation
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Modern networking settings’ growing need for multimedia applications has sparked research into cutting-edge methods to improve network efficiency and resource utilization. A potential model that decouples the control and data planes to allow for centralized management and programmability has been developed called software-defined networking (SDN). The adaptive load optimization technique for multimedia applications with multi-controller utilization in SDN is presented in this research as being novel. The key to this method is its adaptive load optimization mechanism, which intelligently distributes network resources according to current traffic patterns and application needs. The method detects network congestion and proactively redistributes loads across network segments using machine learning and optimization techniques. For multimedia applications, this guarantees optimum resource utilization, reduces latency, and improves Quality of Service (QoS). The suggested approach shows its efficiency in improving the performance of multimedia applications through comprehensive simulations and testing in a variety of network conditions. Results show better throughput, decreased latency, and effective resource utilisation when compared to conventional static load balancing methods. Even in big and complicated network installations, the multi-controller architecture demonstrates its value by maintaining stability and responsiveness.

articleTitle: In-Hospital Mortality Prognosis: Unmasking Patterns using Data Science and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In-hospital mortality prediction is a crucial part of healthcare that can significantly impact patient care strategies and clinical decision-making. Employing Machine Learning (ML) methods in the healthcare domain to improve clinical decision-making and create more effective patient care plans, potentially saves lives. One example is the development of a trustworthy model for forecasting in-hospital mortality. In this work, we make use of a diverse set of patient attributes (features), such as demographics, medical history, and physiological metrics, in order to reveal hidden patterns in the patient data. Our goal is to suggest the best machine learning model that can effectively predict in-hospital mortality, eventually improving patient care outcomes. After investigating 7 ML models, namely; Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest Classifier (RF), Linear Regression (LR), Logistic Regression (LogR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-NN Classifier and Naïve-Bayes Classifier (NB Classifier), we have compared and concluded that the RF model outperforms the other models, providing us with the best accuracy of 92.662%. In the health care domain, it is very much required to explain why and how a particular ML model predicts the specific outcome, to the healthcare professionals. Hence in this work, Explainable AI (XAI) is used to better interpret the RF Classifier, by generating SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) plots.

articleTitle: Compressed ECG Sensing Based RR Interval Measurement for Fast Entropy Analysis of Heart Rate Variability
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of using compressed electrocardiogram (ECG) sensing for R-peak detection in conjunction with entropy-based non-linear heart rate variability (NLHRV) analysis to assess the complexity and irregularity of the heart rate variability (HRV) signal. Non-linear measures offer valuable insights beyond conventional time-domain and frequency-domain features, making them instrumental in understanding these intricate dynamics. In the context of resource-constrained wearable internet of things (IoT) devices, computing HRV parameters from high-resolution (HR) ECG signals presents computational and energy consumption challenges. To address this, compressed ECG sensing for R-peak detection emerges as a promising approach for expedited processing. This study focuses on the application of entropy-based NLHRV analysis to evaluate various clinical and functional conditions using ultra-short-term (1 minute) segments of ECG data. A comparative analysis is presented, employing both compressed ECG sensing for R-peak detection and conventional HR R-peak detection. Specifically, 48 ECG records from the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database (MIT-BIH-AD) and 18 ECG records from the MIT-BIH normal sinus rhythm database (MIT-BIH-NSRD) are used for the analysis. The 7 out of 10 entropy indices have presented more than 85% similar results. These findings signify the applicability of compressed ECG sensing-based entropy measures through NLHRV analysis for rapid health monitoring using ultra-short-term ECG signals.

articleTitle: Power-Efficient FPGA Implementation of SVM for Sleep Apnea Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Sleep apnea is a common sleep disorder characterized by frequent breathing interruptions during sleep, which can lead to a range of negative health consequences. The diagnosis and treatment of sleep apnea require accurate detection of these breathing events, which can be challenging to detect using traditional polysomnography methods. To address this challenge, various automated sleep apnea detection methods have been developed using machine learning techniques. In this research work, we propose the development of a power-efficient and effective Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier for the detection of sleep apnea using Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) technology, which is known for its high processing speed and low power consumption. The SVM classifier is implemented on the Xilinx Nexys Artix-7 FPGA board. Our experimental results show that our proposed SVM classifier achieves high classification accuracy of 98% for testing data, with a low power consumption of 144 mW. This power consumption is significantly less than that of other SVM classifiers executed on a general-purpose processor.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Recent Advances in Observation and Estimation of Nitrogen Oxide (NOx) Emissions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
