articleTitle: Zérosdetect: Phishing URL Detection with Quantum-Driven Zero-shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Phishing, a prevalent cyber danger in contemporary times, involves the fraudulent impersonation of legitimate websites with the intention of deceiving users into divulging confidential information. The insufficiency of classic phishing detection tools has become apparent as fraudsters continue to develop new strategies; these approaches mostly depend on variables such as URL character sequences, site content, and visual resemblance. The present study highlights the “Zérosdetect” approach, a quantum-powered technique for detecting phishing URLs using zero-shot learning, a robust model that makes use of both the zero-shot learning’s adaptability and the computational advantageous nature of quantum computing, it mitigates the need for extensive previous knowledge of phishing URL attributes. In order to detect previously undiscovered phishing attacks, quantum neural network have been deployed to convert URL data into quantum spaces, therefore using the computational benefits of quantum systems. Quantum layers embedded inside Qnodes are a key part of the present system, calculating gradients at a faster pace, optimizing the network performance by rapidly calculating gradients, making the solution both efficient and forward-thinking. The present study lays the groundwork for future cybersecurity initiatives in the era of quantum computing, enhancing the potential to predict new cases of phishing.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Multiband Coplanar Waveguide Fed Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for 5G Sub 6GHz and UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a miniaturized coplanar waveguide-fed frequency-reconfigurable antenna tailored for wireless and 5G Sub-6GHz applications. The antenna design integrates a T-shaped feedline, a rectangular patch, an L-shaped patch, and a modified partial ground plane with a symmetric coplanar waveguide feed, resulting in an impressive performance. The overall prototype dimensions are compact at $23 \times 23.5 \times 1.6$ mm$^{3}$. Frequency reconfiguration is achieved by employing PIN diodes to connect the L-shaped patch and T-shaped feedline. The proposed antenna exhibits Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) and Triple Band responses under different switching conditions, covering a frequency range from 3 GHz to 12 GHz to cover most of the wireless communication frequency range. Extensive simulations reveal outstanding performance metrics, including a simulated efficiency of 96% and a peak gain of 8.61 dB across a maximum bandwidth of 7.6 GHz, accompanied by bidirectional radiation pattern properties. With its compact and cost-effective design, the proposed antenna is a promising solution for enhancing connectivity and signal quality in 5G sub-6GHz and UWB applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Epileptic Seizure Classification using Empirical Mode Decomposition Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Uncontrollable, spontaneous seizures are a hallmark of the neurological condition epilepsy. Epilepsy diagnosis and monitoring frequently include electroencephalogram (EEG) data. It takes time and the skill of a qualified medical professional to interpret EEG data. In order to enhance the diagnosis and treatment of epilepsy, automated approaches for identifying epileptic episodes are required. The empirical mode decomposition (EMD) technique is used in this research to present a deep learning-based strategy for detecting epileptic seizures. The intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) that record various frequency components of the signal are used by the EMD algorithm to decompose EEG signals. We use a Deep Neural Network (DNN) to ascertain whether the input signal has seizure activity or not. The proposed technique improves existing methods, according to our experimental findings, which demonstrate high accuracy.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems using Multilayer Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Smart monitoring ensures that photovoltaic (PV) systems are linked with the grid in a flawless approach. As the use of renewable energy becomes more widespread, increasing PV-grid connection efficiencies will become more important. Real-time data and dynamic control can be achieved by connecting solar power plants to intelligent monitoring systems. In this study, a smart monitoring system based on a Multilayer Neural Network (MLNN) is developed in order to offer precise integration dependability, energy yield, and grid stability in accordance with the load need. The MLNN approach achieves intelligent monitoring in such a way that harmonizes the power generation of PV systems with the fluctuating conditions within the grid.

articleTitle: Speaker Counting by Scattered Microphone Array Based on DOA and Eigenvalue Estimations in Adverse Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a smart subband system for speaker counting is proposed by scattered microphone array (SMA) and using direction of arrival (DOA) estimation with adaptive eigenvalue decomposition (AED). Firstly, the recorded signals by central array are divided into subbands by using gammatone filter bank. Then, the adaptive generalized cross-correlation (GCC) algorithm is implemented on the microphone signals for different subbands. The extracted peaks’ positions are weighted, and this process is repeated on different time frames for spatial sectors in acoustical room. To complete the process, two lateral microphone arrays are considered for verification of the estimated DOAs by using of AED algorithm. The peaks’ positions in the same locations for at least 2 of 3 arrays are considered as the number of overlapped speeches. The proposed speaker counting algorithm by scattered microphone array (SCA-SMA) is compared with other works in adverse environments, which shows the superiority of the presented algorithm in adverse environments.

articleTitle: Quantum Prototype Clustering: Advancing AI Enhanced Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The quantization reconstruction of classical machine learning algorithms is an important research direction in quantum machine learning. Clustering, a widely applied algorithm in machine learning, also holds high research value when quantized. Currently, most quantum machine learning algorithms, including those employing $A I$ techniques, face challenges such as difficulty in replication and the lack of intuitive comparisons with classical algorithms. A quantum prototype clustering algorithm (QPC) is proposed to address these issues, which can be easily deployed on existing general-purpose quantum computing devices. This approach first utilizes single-qubit rotation properties to find the feature mapping with minimal information loss, creating single-qubit rotations from two-dimensional feature data. Then, based on the characteristics of multi-qubit entanglement and entanglement system collapse, a quantum circuit for generating specific quantum entanglement systems and measuring the collapse results of entanglement systems is designed. By establishing the relationship between controlled qubit rotation angles in the entanglement system and the collapse results of the entanglement system and combining the definition of Minkowski distance, a quantum distance is derived for evaluating the similarity of input samples. The quantum distance measurement module, with the same input-output format as the distance calculation module in classical computers, can directly replace the Minkowski distance calculation in prototype clustering without modification, thus reconstructing classical prototype clustering algorithms, with AI included, into QPC. Multiple repeated experiments on publicly available datasets from Kaggle and Scikitlearn demonstrate that with AI integration, QPC exhibits no significant differences in evaluation metrics, such as average sample centre distance, compared to classical prototype clustering algorithms.

articleTitle: Investigating Machine Learning Applications for FDSOI MOS-Based Computer-Aided Design
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: As increasing demand for new applications requires increased demand for integrated chips (ICs), as well as due to miniaturization, the transistor count on a single chip increase to a billion. This produces a lot of data and information during the IC design process, due to which time consumption in the IC design process increases. So, we required technological advancement in this process to speed it up. These all-increase interest in machine learning (ML) in computer-aided design (CAD) tools and processes. This paper provided basic knowledge of ML, its broad application domain in FDSOI, and its use in IC design processes like physical design, mask synthesis, physical verification, lithography, etc.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Circularly Polarized Planar Monopole Antenna for Wireless and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a compact and wideband circularly polarized planar monopole antenna designed for wireless applications and X-Band frequency range, covering 4.1 GHz, 5.8 GHz, 6.5 GHz, and 10 GHz. The proposed antenna utilizes an L-shaped feedline, two slotted patches, a concentric ring, and a modified partial ground plane. The ground plane is enhanced with two extended rectangular protrusions to achieve wideband Circular Polarization (CP) within a compact form factor. The prototype’s overall dimensions are remarkably compact at 0.342$\lambda_{0}\times$ 0.438$\lambda_{0}\times$ 0.022$\lambda_{0}$ ($\lambda_{0}$ at 4.1 GHz). Simulated results indicate an impedance bandwidth of 9.16% (3.96-4.34 GHz) and an impressive 73.34% (5.50-11.87 GHz). Additionally, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 6.10% (3.97-4.22 GHz), 5.98% (6.16-6.54 GHz), and 10.9% (7.07-7.84 GHz) is achieved. The antenna attains a peak gain of 6.7 dB within the operating frequency range. The proposed antenna demonstrates suitability for circular polarization applications in the X-Band and Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) applications, offering a compact yet high-performance solution.

articleTitle: An ECG Signal Compression Technique based on DCT and Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this manuscript, a new ECG signal compression method is proposed with adaptive reconstruction quality. It is based on discrete cosine transformation (DCT) and evolutionary techniques, where DCT is used for the decomposition of original ECG signal. The transformed coefficients are then thresholded using the optimized threshold level. As reconstruction is an essential step in the development of a compression algorithm, it is made adaptive using target-based reconstruction error. Different optimization techniques are utilized for optimizing the threshold level. The exploited techniques in this work are particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO), flower pollination algorithm (FPA), artificial bee colony algorithm (ABC), and cuckoo search algorithm (CS). The encoding of thresholded coefficients is performed by applying the modified run-length encoding (MRLE) technique. The compressed signal is decoded using modified run-length decoding (MRLD), followed by inverse discrete cosine transformation (IDCT). The performance measures used to test the efficiency of this algorithm are compression ratio (CR), percentage root-mean-square difference (PRD), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and quality score (QS). This algorithm focuses on achieving an excellent reconstruction quality along with a good compression ratio. The results show that the ECG signal is compressed effectively with PRD ranging from 1.02 % to 4.95 %, indicating excellent reconstruction.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: An important cause fatalities in the modern era is heart disease. Cardiovascular disease detection is a significant challenge in diagnosis data interpretation. The enormous quantities of data that the medical industry produces sector have shown the value of machine learning for generating estimates and decisions. In order to assess if a person has heart illness or not utilizing a range of data submitted by patients. The necessity to improve diagnostic accuracy and save human resources in hospitals is what inspired us to conduct this research. To diagnose heart disease in our research, we use a number of methods, including Logistic Regression, KNN, Decision Tree Classifier, Random Forest, and SVC, with SVC having the highest accuracy of 89.6%.

articleTitle: Assessment of Different Approaches used for Image Enhancement in Underwater Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: There has been a lot of work done in the field of underwater image processing in recent years. Due to the difficulty of underwater photography, there has been an increase in research in this area. Underwater images frequently suffer from quality decline due to factors like low contrast, blurred features, shifting colors, noise, and variations in the water medium. Improving underwater images is a difficult problem in image processing with many practical implications. In this paper, we present a comprehensive review of the different approaches used for underwater image enhancement. Moreover, we compare different models in terms of accuracy. After that, future research directions have been discussed.

articleTitle: An Effective Path Convergence Approach Founded on Recurrent Ant Colony Optimization (RECACO) in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The new and developing technology known as the Mobile Ad-Hoc Network (MANET) lacks any centralized management and is infrastructure-free with an auto-configuring dynamic topology. Hence, the two main issues with MANETs are network performance and security. In accumulation to the unambiguous criteria of MANET, the QoS necessities that MANET handles comprise bit rate error, path length, interruption, and bandwidth. The causes of the routing problems in MANET include the availability of restricted bandwidth and energy resources. Because nodes have limited energy, link failure, and retransmission will increase as a result. Techniques for energy optimization are applied. In order to optimize energy usage, power-saving approaches should be taken into account. These techniques include minimizing the nodes count needed for multi-cast connectivity, eliminating above panels, and other similar measures. Finding a precise optimal solution in MANETs with a dynamic topology devoid of infrastructure is the first and most crucial problem. Recurrent ant colony optimization has been suggested as a solution to this problem. To achieve optimal path convergence, RECACO recursively performs the actual ant colony approach based on the recurrent value. The RECACO method has been evaluated against a number of current routing protocols. When compared to conventional routing protocols, RECACO saves 0.0026 watt-hours per node and extends the lifespan of the network by 84%. Results from the simulations show that the RECACO algorithm retains more active nodes than the ACO algorithms do over the course of longer simulations.

articleTitle: Quantum Cascade Lasers in Infra-red Absorption Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The primary emphasis of this research paper centers on advancing spectroscopic methods utilizing midinfrared Quantum Cascade Lasers (QCLs). The aim is to apply these techniques in accurately measuring trace gases for environmental science, breath analysis, and determining absolute spectroscopic parameters. In the field of gas-phase analysis, the use of infrared molecular absorption spectroscopy is critical. This technology excels at detecting and tracking minute molecular entities with pinpoint accuracy and selectivity. The study of how electromagnetic (EM) radiation interacts with molecules or atoms, including processes like as absorption, emission, and scattering, is referred to as molecular absorption spectroscopy. Atomic spectroscopy is primarily concerned with quantum transitions manifested as changes in electron configuration. Molecular spectroscopy, on the other hand, studies transitions that occur within a molecule as a result of internal motions such as nuclei vibrations, rotations, and nuclear spin alignment. Because of their intricacy, molecular spectra are more intricate than their atomic counterparts. Furthermore, molecular spectroscopy provides useful information about the molecular framework, such as bond strength, length, the relative arrangement of its constituent atoms, transition dipole moment, and energy levels. These discoveries are made possible by the use of quantum mechanical models that describe the discrete distribution of energy levels within a molecule. This work aims to improve understanding of infrared spectroscopy (IR) by providing a foundational introduction to the principles of molecular spectroscopy. Furthermore, it provides a thorough explanation of commonly used spectroscopic detection techniques for tracking minute air components and trace chemicals in exhaled human breath.

articleTitle: Enhancing Trojan Detection using Machine Learning: Comparative Analysis of Classifier Performance on Embedded Hardware
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In today’s connected world, malware attacks, especially Trojan attacks are rapidly rising. A Trojan is a form of malware that takes on a legitimate piece of software but is malicious and uses the victim’s device to carry out unauthorized tasks. Researchers have created several detecting approaches utilizing machine learning to defend against Trojan assaults. This work compares and assesses the effectiveness of six alternative Trojan detection classifiers using machine learning. The following six classifiers will be utilized: Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Neural Network, and Logistic Regression. Each classifier will be trained and tested using benign and Trojan program samples from a publicly accessible Dataset. This paper will assess the classifiers based on the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The experimentation on the Nvidia Jetson Nano and Raspberry pi hardware platforms to see if the suggested technique can be implemented in resource-constrained settings. The research analyzes different classifiers’ abilities to identify Trojans in machine learning models. The results offer helpful insights for safeguarding machine learning systems in edge computing environments by demonstrating the potency of the suggested technique in identifying Trojans on both Nvidia Jetson Nano and Raspberry Pi.

articleTitle: The Next Frontier: Futuristic Home Control Systems for Modern Living
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: As society progresses into the future, the concept of home control systems has evolved beyond simple automation to become integral to achieving inclusive and sustainable industrialization. This research paper explores the intersection of advanced home control technologies, inclusivity, sustainability, and innovation. It investigates how futuristic home control systems can play a pivotal role in creating smart, eco-friendly, and accessible living environments, ultimately contributing to the realization of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The paper also discusses the potential challenges and opportunities associated with the widespread adoption of such technologies.

articleTitle: Insect Localization and Detection using Object Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent years, the precise localization and detection of insects within images have become increasingly imperative across various domains, including agriculture, entomology, and biodiversity monitoring. Traditional methods for insect identification have heavily relied on manual labor and intricate feature engineering, leading to sub-optimal performance and constrained scalability. Confronted with these formidable challenges, our research paper embarks on an exhaustive investigation into the application of cutting-edge object detection techniques for insect localization and detection. Our specific focus is directed towards the IP102 dataset, a comprehensive and widely acclaimed resource within the field of insect image analysis. The evolution of object detection techniques, particularly those rooted in deep learning, has revolutionized the landscape of computer vision tasks by enabling the simultaneous identification and precise localization of objects within images. Deep learning models, in particular, have demonstrated their prowess in automating insect detection processes and delivering a significant boost in accuracy. Among the plethora of object detection architectures at our disposal, this research harnesses the power various iterations of the YOLO (You Only Look Once) framework, with the results consistently highlighting the superior performance of YOLO versions 5 and 8 in comparison to other models. Further, the incorporation of class activation map (CAM) has played a pivotal role in explaining the exceptional performance of these models.

articleTitle: An AI Decision System to Predict Lung Nodules through Localization from Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The objective of this research is to design an Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision system that helps medical practitioners diagnose lung disease with more probability. Between the 1970s and 1990s, clinical image analysis was carried out by fusing low-level pixel processing (edge and line detectors, region expansion) with mathematical modeling (fitting lines, circles, and ellipses) to develop compound rule-based systems that dealt with particular tasks. In the 1990s the handwritten recognition task adapted Convolutional neural networks(CNN) and achieved the remarkable success that has laid the road for CNNs. The Chinese of Wuhan, in the Hubei Province, saw an epidemic of the coronavirus illness 2019 (COVID-19), which was unleashed by the SARS-CoV-2. The World Health organization declared the pandemic a public health emergency of worldwide significance on January 30, 2020. Over three years have passed since the worldwide struggle against the COVID-19 epidemic began. One of the quickest methods to diagnose patients is to use computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) and deep learning techniques on radiography and radiology images. With this, everyone’s focus has turned to lung disease detection such as tuberculosis and lung cancer through Chest X-ray images with state-of-the-art methods such as CNNs. However, these fail to explain the reason for making such a decision. This work focuses on this aspect of determining region of interest features with a process of localization while predicting lung nodules in two stages with the help of an explainable artificial method.

articleTitle: Home Quarantine Covid-19 Patient’s Monitoring and Prediction Healthcare System using Internet of Things and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Covid-19 infection presents challenges to world in terms of health, mortality, and also socio-economic challenges. The present work provides the detail survey on the various causes for the spread of Covid-19 infection, different technical development to fight against the pandemic, the socia-economic challenges faced during pandemic and impact of Covid-19 spread on economics, education, supply chain, healthcare resources. In this paper an Internet of Things-IoT based wearable device is proposed for monitoring and predicting the health conditions of patient from initial stages of infection till the complete recovery of patient. Machine learning is proposed to be used for predicting the health conditions of Covid-19 infectious patient. The devices so proposed aims to predict the recovery pattern of patient by applying the machine learning to the available Covid-19 patient’s database and zero patient. The present work also provides the various security challenges In IoT systems and role of addressing IoT security challenges.

articleTitle: Contactless HR Measurement from Facial Videos Using Alternative Color Spaces with CEEMDAN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Monitoring vital signs non-invasively by analyzing the blood volumetric variation visible on the skin surface captured in the recorded video frames has recently gained popularity. However, the performance of contactless vital sign measurement can easily deteriorate due to noise interference, resulting in information loss. This paper proposes a new framework for contactless HR measurement. First, in order to improve and retain the image texture quality, a denoising method based on a fractional filter is used. Then, six different color spaces are explored, and the most suitable color channel is chosen from each respective color space to strengthen the cardiac information. The chosen color channels are decomposed using the complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) method followed by the principal component analysis to obtain the pulsatile signal resembling blood volumetric changes. The experimental analysis is performed on two publicly available datasets to assess the efficacy of the proposed approach. The obtained mean absolute error values are 1.57 beats per minute (bpm) for the PURE dataset and 2.11 bpm for the COHFACE dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperformed other state-of-art approaches by providing promising results.

articleTitle: SACF: An Innovative and Secure Architectural Approach for Cybersecurity using Fog Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The significance of cybersecurity cannot be emphasised in a society that is becoming more linked. Unprecedented levels of efficiency and convenience have been made possible by the quick development of digital technology and the proliferation of connected gadgets. But this connectivity has also made people, businesses, and nations more vulnerable to a wide range of online threats. This article examines the complex problems that cybersecurity awareness in our networked society faces and suggests creative solutions to reduce the growing dangers. The article proposed architecture i.e. SACF: Secure Architecture for Cyber security using Fog computing. The article also explores the present threat environment and highlights the various types of cyber attacks. Cybersecurity parameters are also discussed. Thereafter the challenges faced by cybersecurity are discussed, and how these challenges can be overcome is described further. We propose for joint initiatives to elevate cybersecurity awareness as a fundamental and integrated component of our networked society in our conclusion, with a particular focus on the potential contributions of fog computing to boost its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Precision Agriculture using Internet of Things and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The agriculture industry is facing a significant challenge due to poor water management, resulting in a considerable decline in crop production. A lot of water used in irrigation is wasted due to inadequate management practices. The inefficient irrigation systems often have poor water flow control, leading to over-extraction of groundwater, which can lead to harming crop yield. To tackle this problem, precision agriculture, which leverages technology to optimize crop production while minimizing waste and environmental harm, has emerged as a viable solution. IoT-based smart irrigation management systems are an integral part of this approach and can play a vital role in achieving water efficiency goals. In this context, an open-source intelligent system that utilizes machine learning-based algorithms and monitors parameters of soil, such as its moisture and temperature, has been developed to predict the irrigation needs of a field. By forecasting the amount of water required by crops, this system can ensure that the water is utilized more efficiently. The results of the system, which has been successfully deployed on a demo scale, are very promising. The smart system has the potential to revolutionize the way irrigation is managed and help address the water efficiency challenges facing the agriculture industry.

articleTitle: A Smart NIDS Design for SDN-based Cloud IoT Network using Optimal Path Selection and RNN
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has greatly increased the possibility for developing intelligent connections and applications in many facets of daily life. Traditional security solutions frequently fail to solve security issues in cloud-based IoT systems, proving ineffective and insufficient. Software Defined Networking (SDN), which effectively detects and monitors network security vulnerabilities thanks to its programmable characteristics, presents a viable solution to these problems. In order to strengthen computer systems and fend off threats to network security, machine learning (ML) techniques have recently been included into SDN-Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS). Deep learning (DL), one of these cutting-edge ML techniques, has become more popular in the SDN environment. For SDN-based cloud IoT networks, this paper design an efficient path selection system in this study utilizing DL approaches. The strategy comprises employing a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to identify threats and a selection mechanism to pick the best route for data delivery. This study performed tests on two datasets, KDD and UNSWNB15, and the results show that the suggested RNN outperformed existing DL methods by achieving an amazing accuracy ranging from 91% to 95% on both datasets.

articleTitle: Emotion Identification Based on EEG Rhythms Separated using Improved Eigenvalue Decomposition of Hankel Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a framework for identifying emotional state of humans using their electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. The accurate and efficient identification of multiple classes of emotion using non-stationary EEG signals is a challenging task. The emotion identification framework can be developed by applying proper signal processing and machine learning algorithms on the EEG signals. The improved eigenvalue decomposition of Hankel matrix (IEVDHM) is used to decompose the EEG signal into various components. The rhythms are obtained by adding the components together whose mean frequency falls in the range of the respective rhythm. Then from each rhythm, two features are computed namely, permutation min-entropy and Katz fractal dimension measures. Using ensemble subspace k-nearest neighbor (KNN), the feature values are classified into different emotional states namely, happy, sad, fear, and neutral. For testing the performance of the proposed framework, the 10-channel EEG signals were recorded from 39 subjects which include 19 females and 20 males. The average accuracy of 91.30 % is obtained for the proposed framework for human emotion identification using EEG signals. Such emotion identification algorithm can help in obtaining emotional state of the user in brain-computer interface (BCI).

articleTitle: Attention-based Transfer Learning Approach using Spatial Pyramid Pooling for Diagnosis of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A considerable percentage of pregnant women are affected by PCOS, or polycystic ovarian syndrome, a metabolic condition. It causes higher amounts of androgens, or male hormones, and irregular menstrual periods. Follicles, which are tiny sacs packed with fluid that form on the ovaries and impede the regular release of eggs, are a common side effect of PCOS. Initial detection and weight control might help prevent the detrimental effects of PCOS, even though the exact aetiology is still unknown. With the help of the Spatial Pyramid Pooling Network (ASPPNet), a novel attention-based transfer learning approach for PCOS identification from ultrasound pictures is developed in this work. Initially, ResNet-18 is used to extract fundamental features, and the attention module is applied to extract significant disease-related features. Later, the Spatial pyramid pooling technique is utilized to preserve multi-scale features by adopting a fixed-length illustration that is not affected by image size/scale. Spatial pyramid pooling is additionally resistant to image component distortions. The experimental results demonstrate that the ASPPNet exceeds other well-known algorithms with a $\mathbf{9 8 . 7 9 \%}$ accuracy, demonstrating its applicability in both medical and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Parkinson Disease Classification using Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A vast number of people worldwide are afflicted by Parkinson’s disease (PD), a neurological condition. For prompt action to enhance patient outcomes, Parkinson’s disease diagnosis must be made as early and accurately as possible. Hence, this work proposes a hybrid deep learning approach, Convolutional Gated Recurrent Unit (CGRU) method for classification of Parkinson’s disease using varied combinations of features. The work uses a standard dataset retrieved from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and includes voice recordings of people with and without Parkinson’s disease. The work considers the TQWT (Teager-Kaiser energy operator-based Wavelet Transform) features and combines them with Wavelet Transformed-based features and the MFCC (Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients) features. The proposed Convolutional Gated Recurrent Unit (CGRU) model is trained using different combinations of the extracted features namely, only TQWT features, combining TQWT and MFCC features, combining TQWT and Wavelet transformed features, and integrating TQWT, MFCC, and Wavelet transformed features. The suggested model’s performance is assessed using accuracy as the primary metric. The experimental findings show promising classification accuracies ranging between 86% to 96% with TQWD+MFCC to be the best feature combination. The high performance indicates the effectiveness of the hybrid deep learning technique particularly when multiple feature sets are combined.

articleTitle: Ship Detection in Satellite Images using You Only Look Once-Neural Architecture Search
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Ship Detection in remotely sensed satellite imagery is a challenging task due to tiny size of the objects and low resolution of the images. Several object detection methods that perform very well for medium-sized and large-sized objects, miserable fail to perform decently in such applications. From the vast variety of the models available, few You only look once (YOLO) have proven to yield decent efficiency and accuracy in ship detection in satellite images. Hence, the paper proposes to detect and classify ships in remotely sensed satellite images by applying transfer learning to fine-tune the latest YOLO-Neural Architecture Search (YOLO-NAS) model. To the best of our knowledge this paper is the first attempt to test YOLO-NAS model for ship detection in satellite imagery. To demonstrate the strength of the YOLO NAS model, the paper also trains YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 on the same dataset allowing to comprehensively compare the efficiency of the proposed model against previous state-of-art versions. The findings demonstrate high mean average precision scores for the proposed model, indicating the effectiveness of the YOLO-NAS algorithm in accurately locating ships in satellite images.

articleTitle: Development of Acoustic Scene Classification Model using Neural Networks Applied on Reduced Dataset of DCASE
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC) refers to the task of classifying audio signals from various environmental soundscapes into specific predefined classes, such as airports, shopping malls, streets, and more. The goal of ASC is to accurately identify the acoustic scene associated with a given audio file, which has practical applications in fields like audio analysis and environmental monitoring. This paper focuses on ASC task, aiming to surpass the DCASE 2021 Challenge Task 1 - Subtask A baseline model’s accuracy of 47.7%. Ten diverse audio classes are considered using the TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2020 Mobile dataset. Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is applied to reduce the dataset to 9,225 audio files, preserving vital information. Two models, CNN and RNN, leveraging Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) features, are developed and trained. This paper also emphasizes the importance of a structured JSON file, named “data,” which encapsulates essential dataset details, including mappings, MFCC features, and labels. This structured representation not only enhances efficiency but also simplifies the training of both CNN and RNN models. The CNN achieves around 54.14% accuracy, while the RNN excels with an accuracy of approximately 55.12%. The proposed models significantly outperform the baseline model, indicating their effectiveness in ASC.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis for Better User Experience in Tourism Chatbot using LSTM and LLM
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Emotions of human plays a vital role in the usage of any technical solutions. AI now provide various opportunity to devise solutions that can understand human emotion from written and spoken words. In this research, we focus on the importance and application of sentiment analysis for an AI chatbot designed for tourism. The chatbot helps to act as a real-time information service system for tourists visiting a new city. Incorporating sentiment analysis to identify the user’s emotions and framing the response catering to the user’s emotions can enhance the chatbot’s user experience. By integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Large Language Models (LLM), this study aims to offer the components of a comprehensive system that understands and responds to user sentiments, enhancing the tourism experience.

articleTitle: Designing a Customized Communication System using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work focuses on creating a personalized communication system tailored to the unique needs of individuals with visual impairments, using the versatile Raspberry Pi microcomputer. The goal is to improve accessibility and communication by incorporating innovative features and technologies. The system's central functionality is built around the Raspberry Pi, making use of its computational power and connectivity options. A camera module is integrated to capture visual information, and advanced image recognition techniques are applied to extract meaningful content from the captured images. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology is then employed to convert visual information into text. To facilitate effective communication, the system includes text-to-speech conversion capabilities, utilizing the Raspberry Pi's processing power to transform written text into spoken words. This ensures that individuals with visual impairments can receive information in an auditory format, enhancing their accessibility to written content. The design emphasizes simplicity, user-friendliness, and portability to enable individuals with visual impairments to easily carry and operate the system in various settings. Additionally, considerations for power efficiency are integrated, including potential solutions for battery-powered operation to enhance mobility.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Methods Using Linear and Non-Linear Models with PTT and PR Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) variability is linked with heart diseases, stroke, kidney failure, diabetes, and sleep apnea which are the leading cause of deaths worldwide. Continuous measurement of BP plays a vital role in timely detecting hypertension and hypotension and enabling accurate and reliable diagnosis and treatment of life-threatening diseases. Compared to the traditional sphygmomanometer and automatic oscillometric cuff BP measurement methods, cuffless BP measurement device can enable continuous measurement of systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP (DBP) in daily life without any disturbance, that play a major role in effective monitoring and controlling of hypertension. In this paper, we study the performance of linear and non-linear BP estimation models based on the pulse transit time (PTT) and pulse rate (PR) for measuring SBP, DBP, and mean arterial pressure (MAP). We demonstrate the reliability of the estimated SBP and DBP values by finding the MAP error computed between the estimated MAP using the MAP model and the MAP calculated directly using the estimated SBP and DBP values. The performance of the BP estimation methods is evaluated using the MIMIC database in terms of mean absolute error (MAE), Bland-Altman ratio (BAR), and BP estimation error range metric. Evaluation results showed that the non-linear BP estimation model performs better than the linear model. Results further showed that BP estimation models highly demand accurate estimation of PTT and PR from electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals which is challenging under different kinds of artifacts.

articleTitle: Case Study of Image Feature Extraction using Conventional and Deep Learning Methods: Autoencoder and U-Net
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a brief review of traditional and deep learning techniques and classification of images. The conventional methods increase classification and feature extraction design, that turn improved texture, color and, shape feature performance. Handcrafted features are required by traditional feature extraction methods. In order to extract new features from the training data, deep learning is used. While supervised learning still makes up many current deep learning implementations, unsupervised learning is progressively taking its place in order to deal with data (real-world) without manual human interaction. This paper also outlines the famous unsupervised deep learning algorithms for feature extraction such as Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBM), Autoencoder and, Deep Belief Network (DBN) first, then shows some open challenges of deep learning. A deep learning algorithms autoencoder and U-net model are used as an example in this study to extract features from images. It explains how, even though u-net outperforms convolutional autoencoder in terms of performance, convolutional autoencoder (AE) generated features generate higher accuracy when applied to classifiers. Authors have been used RNNs or its variants (LSTM, Peephole connection, GRU) with CNN as a hybrid model to achieve remarkable effects in image captioning. Following the success of these remarkable outcomes, the attention mechanism developed. A detailed and updated review discussed and several approaches, evaluation metrics, and applications have been presented in the literature.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation on Various Routing Strategies in IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The term “Internet of Things” (IoT) is used to signify a global network of common objects furnished with sensors, processors, and network connections. Gateways facilitate the collection and transmission of data among these devices and the internet. Routing solutions facilitate communication between IoT devices so that data may flow smoothly. In the context of the IoT, “routing” is a computation used to transmit information from one place in a network to another. The timely and accurate transmission of data is dependent on effective routing between IoT devices, other devices, and central systems. Network size, device capabilities, energy limits, and communication patterns are only some of the considerations that lead to the deployment of a particular routing protocol or strategy in an IoT network. In this paper, an attempt has been made to present various routing strategies used in IoT. Furthermore, we discuss IoT layer architecture. Further, provide performance analysis on various hierarchal routing protocols using MATLAB. Numerous IoT devices, including batteries, are constrained by limited power resources. The implementation of hierarchical routing can contribute to energy conservation through the reduction of data processing and communication demands on individual devices. The performance is evaluated based on the total number of alive nodes and dead nodes. At last, we addressed the future directions of routing in the IoT.

articleTitle: Detection of Epileptic Seizures by Analysis of Electroencephalogram based on Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent years, some novel methods have been developed for the detection of diseases based on biomedical signals. In this article, a method for the automated detection of epilepsy seizures is presented by analyzing electroencephalogram (EEG) signals based on the wavelet transform. In the first step, the EEG signals are pre-processed with the Savitzky-Golay filters (SGF) for noise elimination. The filtered signals are decomposed with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to construct spontaneous alpha and beta brain rhythms. The mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, energy and entropy characteristics are extracted from healthy and seizure intervals. By using support vector machine (SVM), the signals are classified in the categories of normal and epileptic, reaching precision levels of 92.82% in the alpha rhythm in comparison with other previous works.

articleTitle: Improving Diabetes Management with Support Vector Machine based Fundus Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Diabetes poses a widespread health concern and, when left untreated, can lead to costly complications. Fundus imaging serves as a crucial tool in diabetes monitoring by identifying retinal abnormalities that could have severe consequences. However, the challenge arises from the absence of standardized databases and evaluation protocols among various research groups that have proposed fundus image analysis algorithms. This lack of standardization makes it challenging to assess the accuracy and reliability of these algorithms. In medical diagnosis, the evaluation of disease classification accuracy commonly relies on sensitivity and specificity measures. In the context of diabetic retinopathy, sensitivity and specificity are evaluated on a preimage basis for fundus images. Support-vector machine (SVM) classifiers have proven effective in detecting abnormalities in fundus images. This paper introduces an innovative approach that combines descriptive features of flow areas to enhance the robustness of results in the presence of phase noise and multiple scattering. The proposed approach, utilizing an SVM classifier, achieved higher levels of sensitivity and specificity compared to existing methods. This tool holds significant potential for aiding in the early detection and treatment of diabetic retinopathy and could be seamlessly integrated into non-invasive screening tools. To further enhance the accuracy and reliability of fundus image analysis algorithms, the adoption of standardized evaluation protocols and representative fundus image databases is imperative.

articleTitle: Driving into the Future: A Comparative Analysis of the Hough Transform and Convolutional Neural Network for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper conducts a comparative analysis of two lane detection algorithms, the Hough Transform and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), within real-world scenarios using camera and Raspberry Pi technology. A comprehensive prototype is developed, integrating both hardware and software components. The algorithms’ results are categorized as “pass” or “fail,” and accuracy is determined by comparing the number of “pass” cases to the total cases. This research effectively discerns the conditions in which each algorithm excels, providing valuable insights for practical implementation. It aids in selecting the most suitable algorithm for specific environmental and operational conditions, advancing the field of lane detection.

articleTitle: Heart Guardian: A Model for Predicting Cardiovascular Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Heart disease is a major cause of mortality worldwide and timely detection and intervention being essential to enhancing patient health condition. Recently, deep learning techniques, have shown promising results in various healthcare applications. In this paper, we present a novel deep learning-based model for heart disease prediction that leverages a diverse range of risk factors, medical imaging data, and patient demographics. The proposed model utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for extraction of features from the medical images, which are then fused with the other risk factors and fed into a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for classification. Deep learning techniques are used to provide insights into the features contributing to the predictions, enhancing the interpretability and transparency of our model. The performance of the model is evaluated using the real-world data set of patients with and without heart disease and compare it to traditional risk assessment approaches. Our study adds to the expanding body of literature on deep learning’s potential in the healthcare industry, highlighting the transformative impact of these models in improving heart disease prediction and enabling personalized interventions. Our findings show that the suggested model performs better than others in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, outperforming traditional risk assessment methods.

articleTitle: Efficient e-KYC Authentication System: Redefining Customer Verification in Digital Banking
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: e-KYC is an abbreviation for the digitization, electronic, and online notion of KYC techniques. e-KYC (electronic know Your Customer) is a paperless technique that reduces the fees and forms required in KYC operations. The e-KYC procedure is a virtual and remote translation of the traditional KYC procedure. Weeks of waiting have resulted in seconds with a significantly reduced charge in an optimized way. To ensure that e-KYC approaches fulfil the same security criteria as traditional identity and face verification, digital identification processes with high levels of safety and reliability should be used. The goal is to build a website with the assistance of machine learning that uses optical character recognition (OCR), face recognition, and face verification algorithms to make it easier for customers to validate their credentials for banking purposes such as opening a bank account, applying for a loan, and other business purposes. This will accelerate the KYC process phenomenally. Customers have the option to update their KYC information on the designated website. This can be done by completing the KYC form, which requires providing personal details such as name, Aadhaar card and PAN card numbers. Additionally, customers are required to submit a photograph of their AADHAAR Card or PAN Card, as well as upload a ten-second real-time video of their face. The website utilizes OCR, face recognition, and face verification algorithms to perform e-KYC verification for Indian citizen, resulting in time efficient manner.

articleTitle: Efficient Image Feature Extraction through Simultaneous Training of Nested U-Nets
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the last few decades, coarse-graining emerged as a tool in various fields to optimize the speed-accuracy complexity of a system and extract prominent features from it. But, in the field of image processing, its application and advancement are not well understood. Moreover, in image processing, the development of optimal neural architecture and its classification are performed on databases with structured and standard images. Here, a computationally efficient CG model is introduced that is very effective in re-scaling and classification of unstructured images. The research and developments in the field of image processing are primarily focused on the development of new tools and network architecture in order to optimize accuracy, whereas the training process remains trivial. With an increase in complexity, the number of layers, and the use of multiple network models in the system, this training process becomes computationally inefficient and costs its accuracy. Here, a unique method is also provided to combine multiple models together as a single network architecture and train them together as a single model rather than doing it separately for every model.

articleTitle: State Modeling and Verification of Solar Energy Harvesting System for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The increasing popularity of using renewable energy emerges as a leading sustainable solution in the energy domain. Recently, energy harvesting, as a promising technology, uses ambient energy sources from nature to power IoT devices. For example, solar energy holds immense potential from the energy sources as it is abundantly available in the Earth’s atmosphere. While practical applications of energy harvesting systems in real-life scenarios exist, it is essential to verify these systems formally. This paper presents a comprehensive model followed by verifying a solar energy harvester system. Each proposed solar energy harvesting system component is transformed into respective finite state models. The details are then formally verified using model checking, a powerful formal verification technique. The specifications that ascertain desired properties serve as a foundation for evaluating the performance of the designed solar energy harvesting system.
